description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; U; PPC Mac OS X 10.4; en; rv:1.9.0.18) Gecko/2010021619 Camino/2.0.2 (like Firefox/3.0.18)

Feel free to close this bug if this is not the right place for this information.

I'm currently working on a migration from the SourceForge bugtracker to Bugzilla.  Our current attitute is not very demanding regarding the import of bugs; anything that improves from no import at all is better.  This results in the scripts/procedure laid out here not to be a perfect 1-to-1 migration.

Maybe this information is interesting enough to put somewhere in some documentation place (a wiki, wherever) such that others can benefit from the steps I've made to get this far.

We started with the XML dump from the sourceforge project as can be done by an administrator.  It includes a lot more than just the tracker items.

On this XML file, I ran the xslt proc as I will attach.  It basically selects the tracker items out of the file and transforms them to the format that Bugzilla (version 3.6) exports itself for bugs.  The proc does a very lazy map of the status and resolutions from sourceforge to Bugzilla's one.  If you added any, it probably needs tweaking.

% xsltproc --novalid --nodtdattr sf2bz.xslt monetdb_export.xml > bugzilla-sfbugs.xml

Because I failed to format timestamps in the xslt translation, this is done afterwards with an AWK script.  Since it's processing anyway, at the same time email addresses can be converted, if required.

% awk -f bzpostprocess.awk bugzilla-sfbugs.xml > bugzilla-final-sfbugs.xml

Next the bugzilla-final-sfbugs.xml can be imported with importxml.pl tool from Bugzilla.  Bug #562308 and bug #562314 contain enhancements that make the import result look nicer.  E.g.:

% ./importxml.pl --post_comments --bug_page="tracker.php?aid=" bugzilla-final-sfbugs.xml

This would do the normal import, but recreate all comments as real comments, and create working links/references to the original bug on SourceForge.  E.g.:

  This bug was previously known as _bug_ 602271 at
  http://sourceforge.net/support/tracker.php?aid=602271

**Description:** A set of scripts and procedures have been developed for migrating data from SourceForge to Bugzilla (version 3.6). To enhance the security of Bugzilla over HTTPS, we propose the inclusion of Strict Transport Security (STS) headers on HTTPS responses. summary: Tagging comments as bug/todo, fixed, verified, question, answer, split
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux i686; en-US) AppleWebKit/533.6 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/5.0.380.0 Safari/533.6
Build Identifier: 3.0.4

We have a modified version of Bugzilla 3.0.4 where you can tag specific comments as bugs or todos (also auto-reopens a non-open bug) which can then be tagged as fixed and then be tagged as verified.

I know some will find this odd but others may like thinking about it as new bugs vs new comments being like new processes vs new threads. It's very heavy to create a new bug compared to just commenting and reopening the same bug with a comment.

This is all client-side javascript. Nothing interacts with the database. It is only meant to improve comprehension and organization and trackability while moving through the design, development, and QA stages of a particular bug.

We can also tag a comment as a question which can then be answered.

Comments can be tagged as split by which you indicate that its content has moved to another location (as indicated in the comment that does the splitting).

Tags appear in the comment header line like this:

------- Comment #118 From John Doe 2010-04-29 20:04:54 - [Reply] [Bug] [Fixed] [Verified] -------

Each tag has a color attempting to match bugzilla's typical colors for the same meaning.. Bug/TODO are red. Fixed is orange. Verified is green.

Hovering over a tag will indicate what comment made the tag. Clicking the tag will take you directly to the comment that made the tag also block highlighting the comment text with a similar color to the tag.

The example comment header above may be caused by a sequence like:

1. New comment:

 > Bug: This is a bug because of x, y and z.

2. New comment:

 > #118: Fixed.
 > 
 > Wups this bug was caused by a typo!

3. New comment:

 > #118: Verified
 > 
 > X, y and z are now fixed.

Finally, we have reports as links, in the "Related actions" boxes, that open in a new window and display the comments that are Unfixed, Unverified, or Open (includes unfixed, unverified and unanswered). This is a great way to make sure you've covered all your bases when deciding whether a bug is really fixed and verified.

We find these improvements to be a vast gain in efficiency, organization and comprehension of the related bugs.

It's also a great, quick visual way of running over a bug and seeing if there are any bugs, todos, or unfixed, unverified, or unanswered items left.

We know that Mozilla would do a great job building and enhancing such a feature.

I'd be happy to answer any questions about processes or quirks about using comment tagging.

**Feature Request:** Comment Tagging and Tracking System

**Purpose:** Improve comprehension, organization, and trackability of bug comments throughout the design, development, and QA stages by introducing a tagging system for comments.

* No database interactions.
* Customized to improve bug management processes.

**Bugzilla-Queue Init Script Enhancement**

To enhance compatibility with SuSE systems, we propose modifying the bugzilla-queue init script to conform to Linux Standard Base (LSB) format. This will enable seamless integration and operation on LSB-compliant distributions.

The updated init script should include the following functionality:

* Start: initiate the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon
* Stop: terminate the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon
* Restart: restart the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon
* Try-restart: attempt to restart the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon if it is not running
* Force-reload: reload the configuration of the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon
* Reload: reload the configuration of the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon without interrupting service
* Status: display the status of the Bugzilla jobqueue daemon

A patch, conforming to LSB specifications, will be provided as a solution. This enhancement is essential for ensuring seamless operation on SuSE systems and other LSB-compliant distributions.

description:
Bugzilla quicksearch currently searches Alias field (without letting the user know in the summary on top of result list), but we only search for full matches in that field. Partial matches would be helpful, too, and they won't hurt those who know the exact alias which will still take them straight to the bug.

STR

0 Bug 544553 currently has the alias "BugzillaForHumans"

1 You are looking for existing bugs relating to your problem
1a) with no knowledge about the alias (just searching for relevant bugs)
1b) with partial knowledge about the alias ("was it BugzillaForPeople, or BugzillaForStarters?")
1c) with full knowledge about the alias
 
2 You are doing bugzilla quicksearches
2a) https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/buglist.cgi?quicksearch=bmo for humans
2b) https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/buglist.cgi?quicksearch=bugzillafor
2c) https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/buglist.cgi?quicksearch=bugzillaforhumans

Actual result

2a) quicksearch=bmo for humans
-> this will actually find the bug, but only because of the bug's title. If "humans" was a relevant word that happens to be NOT in the title, but ONLY in the alias, we wouldn't find anything (this bug).

2b) quicksearch=bugzillafor
-> this will not find the bug, as the last part of the alias is missing and we are only finding exact matches for the alias (this bug)

2c) quicksearch=bugzillaforhumans
-> only searching for the exact alias will return the bug (and take you right there, as it should)

Expected result

2a), 2b) quicksearch=bmo for humans / quicksearch=bugzillafor
-> this should find the bug (and display a result list), based on partial match of "humans" or "bugzillafor" compared against the value of the alias field: "BugzillaForHumans"
-> if it's only one match, take me straight to the bug

2c) quicksearch=bugzillaforhumans
-> searching for the exact alias will return the bug, and take me right there (as it does now)

Rationale: We often give alias names to important meta bugs.
- We should make it easier for average users to discover these (and work their way forward from there, avoid duplicates etc.)
- and we should make it easier for advanced users to find aliases they know of but don't remember the exact wording or spelling

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request:** Enhance Bugzilla Quicksearch to Return Partial Matches for Alias Field

**Description:**

The Bugzilla quicksearch feature should be modified to return partial matches when searching the Alias field. Currently, only exact matches are returned, which can make it difficult for users to discover aliases they may know by name but not exactly.

**Problem Statement:** When performing a quicksearch using an alias with partial knowledge (e.g., "bugzillafor" instead of "bugzillaforhumans"), the search does not return any results if the exact alias is not used. This hinders the discovery and use of aliases, which are often given to important meta bugs.

**Expected Behavior:** The quicksearch should return partial matches for the Alias field, allowing users with partial knowledge of an alias to still find relevant bugs. If only one match exists, the user should be taken directly to that bug.

**Rationale:** This enhancement aims to make it easier for both average and advanced users to discover aliases they may know by name but not exactly. By returning partial matches, users can more easily find and work with important meta bugs, reducing duplicate efforts and improving overall efficiency.

summary: Refactor See Also to use separate modules for each type of URL
description:
Right now, add_see_also has a bunch of code in an if/else tree, that determines which types of URLs are valid. Instead, we should have a class heirarchy like this:

  Bugzilla::BugUrl
  Bugzilla::BugUrl::Bugzilla
  Bugzilla::BugUrl::Bugzilla::Local
  Bugzilla::BugUrl::Launchpad
  Bugzilla::BugUrl::Google

Bugzilla::BugUrl would currently implement two methods:

  should_handle

  This takes a string and returns 1 or 0. It returns 1 if this particular module should be the one to parse the input string, and 0 otherwise. (So, we go through all of the Bugzilla::BugUrl subclasses we have available, and we pick the first one that returns 1.)

  Bugzilla::Object create/run_create_validators/etc.

  Bugzilla::Bug::add_see_also can call Bugzilla::BugUrl::${class}::check_required_create_fields and Bugzilla::BugUrl::${class}::run_create_validators, and that way they will validate the url. (this is the same as what the current code in the if/else in add_see_also does)

  Then, Bugzilla::Bug::update can call Bugzilla::BugUrl::${class}::insert_create_data to insert the stored BugUrl objects. (Much the same as how we update the bug_see_also table now.)

  Of course, as part of this, $bug->see_also will have to start returning BugUrl objects. We may also have to start storing which subclass is being used for each URL in the see_also table.


  This will allow the See Also system to be easily extendable, and we can add a hook to extend it, in a separate bug.

**Feature Request:** Modularize URL Handling in Bugzilla's See Also System

The current implementation of `Bugzilla::Bug::add_see_also` employs an if/else tree to determine valid URL types. To improve modularity, maintainability, and extensibility, we propose introducing a hierarchical class structure for handling different URL types.

**Key Components:**

1. **Class Hierarchy:** Introduce subclasses under `Bugzilla::BugUrl`, each representing a specific URL type (e.g., `Bugzilla::BugUrl::Bugzilla`, `Bugzilla::BugUrl::Launchpad`, etc.). 
2. **`should_handle` Method:** Implement this method in the base class, `Bugzilla::BugUrl`, to determine whether it should handle a given input string.
3. **Validator Methods:** Move validation logic for each URL type to their respective subclasses (e.g., `check_required_create_fields`, `run_create_validators`).
4. **Data Insertion:** Modify `Bugzilla::Bug::update` to call the corresponding insertion method in the subclass associated with each stored `BugUrl` object.
5. **Object Return:** Update `$bug->see_also` to return instances of `BugUrl` objects, including metadata on the specific subclass used for each URL.

**Goals:**

* Improve modularity and maintainability by separating URL handling logic
* Enable easy extension of the See Also system through subclasses and hooks
* Enhance data integrity and consistency by using validator methods

This refactored implementation will provide a more modular, flexible, and scalable foundation for the Bugzilla's See Also system.

The `SHOW TABLE STATUS` query within the `checksetup` process is experiencing significant performance issues on large databases, resulting in slow execution times (approximately 5 seconds with a cold cache and 3 seconds with a warm cache).

To optimize this query, it has been discovered that using the following equivalent query against the `information_schema.TABLES` table yields significantly faster results:

summary: "CC list" is not a typical term for most issue trackers/webapps other than webmail, should use more common web app jargon
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; U; Intel Mac OS X 10.6; de; rv:1.9.2.12) Gecko/20101026 Firefox/3.6.12
Build Identifier: Bugzilla 3.4.6

As a user of an opensource software, i sometimes come across bugs or problems, that already have been reported. If i find the bugreport, i sometimes want to get a notification (via email), if there are any updates for this issue.

For example, in Launchpad.net, i click on "subscribe". In lighthouseapp.com, i click on "watch ticket". It works like on Twitter.com where i click on "follow".

For bugzilla this is not that easy, at least for me. I think, i have to check the "Add me to CC list"-checkbox  and then click "commit" at the top of the page. But i am not really shure. I did that, but all it told me, was something like "yxz@example.com got notified, excluding ME and another person".

I think one problem is the term CC List. I get that "CC" means something like the "CC" in my email app, but i think the use in bugzilla is misleading.
I think the term "CC List" is already learned by people who are already familiar with bugzilla and it's vocabulary, but to new users, who want to get involved, it does not make a lot of sense.

So given if my assumptions about that "Add me to CC list" actually subscribes me to report update aren't false, i got three problems:
1. The term "CC List"
2. The feedback, after having subscribed to a report
3. (Maybe minor) I have to click the "commit" button, but i just want to get notified about… maybe other people commiting something…


Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Visit any report
2. Look for a way to subscribe to updates for this report

Actual Results:

**Request:** Improve Subscription Notification Process in Bugzilla

**Description:**

To facilitate user engagement and involvement, we propose enhancing the subscription notification process on Bugzilla. The goal is to provide users with an intuitive way to receive updates on existing bug reports.

**Problem Statement:**

Currently, Bugzilla's terminology and functionality may confuse new users who are accustomed to more conventional issue tracking workflows. Specifically:

* The term "CC List" is unfamiliar to many users, and its meaning in the context of Bugzilla is unclear.
* The feedback provided after subscription is ambiguous, leading to uncertainty about what subscribing entails.
* The current process requires multiple steps, including clicking the "commit" button, which may not be immediately clear for users seeking notification-only functionality.

**Objective:**

To address these issues, we aim to:

1. Update terminology to align with industry-standard web app jargon.
2. Revise the subscription process to provide clear and concise feedback upon successful subscription.
3. Simplify the user experience by reducing unnecessary steps in the subscription workflow.

**Reproducibility:** This issue is reproducible on all Bugzilla instances, as it pertains to a fundamental aspect of user engagement and interaction with bug reports.

summary: Add user 'capabilities' to Bugzilla
description:
At the moment, we have params like "insidergroup" and "chartgroup". But we don't have e.g. a "quipseditinggroup" or a "quipsmoderatinggroup". In several places, the code hard-codes a particularly capability (such as editing quips) to a particular group (such as 'admin'). Any time an installation want to slice and dice the permissions differently, they have to edit the code.

Instead, we should have a set of capabilities, which are quite fine-grained - edit_quips, add_quips, create_charts, etc., plus an administrator-defined map from capabilities to groups. The code would directly check capabilities rather than group membership, and the map would be used to map to the relevant group.

So e.g. instead of $user->in_group('bz_canusewhines'), the code would do $user->can('usewhines'), and there would be an admin-controlled mapping which mapped the "usewhines" capability to the "bz_canusewhines" group - or the "admin" group, or the "editbugs" group, or whatever the admin wanted.

This would mean, for example, bmo wouldn't need to edit the code to change quip moderation from admins to members of 'quip-moderators', or blessing all groups from 'editusers' to 'admin'.

Gerv

**Request:** Introduce Capabilities-Based Access Control in Bugzilla

**Description:**

To enhance flexibility and customization, we propose implementing capabilities-based access control. This will involve introducing fine-grained capabilities (e.g., edit_quips, add_quips, create_charts) that are mapped to specific groups by administrators.

Instead of relying on hardcoded group membership checks, the system will directly verify user capabilities. An administrator-defined mapping will allow for flexible assignment of capabilities to various groups, enabling customized permission configurations without requiring code modifications.

**Changes:**

* Introduce a set of fine-grained capabilities
* Implement capability-based access control instead of group membership checking
* Allow administrators to map capabilities to specific groups through a customizable mapping system

This change will enable bugzilla installations to easily adapt permissions and roles according to their specific needs, without requiring code edits.

description:
Time spent in searching the database can be broken down into basically these things:

1) The query analysis and parsing done by the database engine.
2) The actual locating of data using the parsed query.
3) The actual delivery of data from the database to Bugzilla.
4) The rendering of the results.

Of these, it's 3+4 that actually take most of the time--1+2 are usually almost instantaneous.

Most people rarely need to see more than 500 results in a search, at the most.

So, to speed up searches, we can, by default, limit every search to 500 results. Then if there are more results (which we can know by doing an actual database-side limit of 501) we can provide a link on the buglist that will re-run the query and have it display *all* the results (but subject to the limit set by bug 632717).

summary: Redesign custom search to be an independent series of logical clauses (AND/OR)
description:
Here's my original description of this enhancement, from when I proposed it on the developers list:

    So, the Boolean Charts are great, they're powerful, and they've been an important part of Bugzilla since 2000. However, the Boolean Charts have some problems:

	* The way that AND, OR, and multiple charts work is really confusing. I didn't fully understand it until I fully understood Search.pm, which very few people understand.

	* You can't really do arbitrary AND/OR groupings. For example, there's
no way to do this search with the Boolean Charts:

	(a AND b) OR (c AND d)

	* They generate extremely long URLs, because the URL parameters look
like field0-0-0, type0-0-0, and value0-0-0. Sometimes these URLs are too long for the web server to deal with, and people can't do the searches they want to.


	As such, I'd like to propose a redesign of what we currently call "boolean charts" into a system that is able to do arbitrary logical groupings. Here's how it will work:

	URL parameters will look like:

	f1=bug_id&o1=equals&v1=1234&j2=OR&n2=1&f2=short_desc&o2=substring&v2=test

	"f" means "field", "o" means "operator", "v" means "value", "j" means
"join" (either AND or OR), and "n" means "not". That URL is a search for
bugs where:

	the bug_id equals 1234
	OR NOT (the summary contains the string "test").

	There will be two "special" fields for the "f" parameter: OP and CP,
which mean "open paren" and "close paren". These will allow logical groupings, with an infinite amount of nesting. For example, if you want to do:

	( (bug_id = 1 AND short_desc = 'a') OR NOT (bug_id = 2 AND short_desc =
'b') ) AND priority = 'Low'

	The URL would look like (split on to multiple lines, indented,  and
with & removed to help readability):

	f1=OP
		f2=OP
			f3=bug_id o3=equals v3=1
			j4=AND
			f4=short_desc o4=equals v4=a
		f5=CP
		j6=OR n6=1
		f6=OP
			f9=bug_id o9=equals v9=2
			j10=AND
			f10=short_desc o10=equals v10=b
		f11=CP
	f12=CP
	j13=AND
	f13=priority o13=equals v13=Low

	And even with all that extra OP/CP/AND/OR stuff, I'm pretty sure the
resulting URL is still shorter than the equivalent boolean charts URL (which would be impossible anyway).

	* The boolean chart UI will get two new buttons: "(" and ")". The "Add
a new chart" button will be removed.

	* Certain fields like "flags" want to all refer to the same flag if you
specify multiple criteria. For example, if you search for "Flags equals review?" AND "Flag Requestee equals mkanat", you probably mean "find me bugs where the review flag has a requestee of mkanat". In the new system, this will be accomplished by "associating" any fields that are within parens. (Formerly, this was accomplished by associating any fields within the same chart, which could be pretty confusing for users.) So within any set of parens, all searches for the Flag fields will be about one flag.
	Alternately, we could come up with some specific mechanism for people to associate things, which might be better, but I'm not thinking of anything that would be simple enough in the code and the UI other than the system I just proposed.

	* Adding a different "join" than the previous "join" without specifying
an "open-paren" would be an error. That is, this is too ambiguous to allow: a AND b OR c AND d. Did the user intend "(a AND b) OR (c AND d)", or did they intend "a AND (b or C) AND d"?
	The UI will handle this automatically by closing the existing parentheses set if you specify a different operator than you last used.
It will still be possible to generate improper URLs, though, which should be throw an error to prevent unexpected results from ambiguous logical groupings.

	* Saved Searches and New Charts series can both be upgraded to this new
system automatically, most likely with no loss of functionality, within the "convert_old_params" method in Search.pm, so there should be little need for people to manually fix their saved searches or any URLs that they have linked to Bugzilla using the old system. We may be able to do something similar to continue supporting people's Default Queries, if they involve boolean charts, but that's a lower priority.

	* Once the system is in place, QuickSearch can be upgraded to support
parentheses. We will need some better parsing code to support this properly, possibly using some CPAN module.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Redesign Custom Search with Independent Logical Clauses (AND/OR)**

The custom search functionality in Bugzilla will be redesigned to allow for independent logical clauses (AND/OR) and improved URL handling. This enhancement aims to address current limitations and complexities in the Boolean Charts system.

Key Features:

* **Arbitrary AND/OR Groupings**: Users can create complex searches with multiple levels of nesting, using parentheses to group conditions.
* **Improved URL Parameters**: The new system will use a more intuitive parameter format, making it easier for users to understand and generate URLs.
* **Enhanced UI**: The boolean chart UI will be modified to include "( )" buttons and remove the "Add a new chart" button.
* **Association of Fields within Parens**: When searching for multiple criteria related to flags or other fields, the system will automatically associate them within parentheses.

Benefits:

* Simplified search logic and improved user experience
* Reduced complexity in URL handling and generation
* Seamless upgrade of Saved Searches and New Charts series with minimal disruption to existing functionality

Technical Requirements:

* The "convert_old_params" method in Search.pm will be modified to support the new system.
* Additional parsing code may be required for QuickSearch to properly support parentheses.

This redesign aims to provide a more user-friendly and efficient search experience, while maintaining compatibility with existing features and saved searches.

To enhance the user experience during maintenance mode, it is proposed to modify the server's behavior when returning a 503 Service Unavailable status code. summary: Don't force line-wrapping breaks in comments; use fixed-width styling instead
description:
Currently Bugzilla forces line-wrapping breaks in comments after a line has reached a certain number of characters. This overrides the (likely superior) parsing that the browser would do and it prevents useful copying and pasting of the comment to other places. It also can mess with the formatting of comments that have already specified manually where line breaks should happen, as well as text parsing that doesn't expect free-flowing text to have arbitrary, forced line breaks.

I don't know if this is hard-coded or just a styling issue, but I think Bugzilla should get out of the forced–line-wrapping business and allow the browser to do its own wrapping. If a particular width is desired for the comments (rather than allowing them to take up the whole width of the window), then the element can be styled in CSS to maintain a given width.

(This may be related to bug 641913, but I think the proposed implementation is different.)

summary: Require Perl 5.10.1
description:
In October 1999, Bugzilla 2.8 required Perl 5.4.
In August 2001, Bugzilla 2.16 required Perl 5.5 (bug 97721).
In October 2002, Bugzilla 2.18 required Perl 5.6 (bug 173495).
In March 2006, Bugzilla 3.0 required Perl 5.8 (bug 314470).
In August 2007, Bugzilla 3.2 required Perl 5.8.1 (bug 361149).
In 2012 or 2013, maybe Bugzilla 5 or 6 will require Perl 5.10.1?

There are some nice features in Perl 5.10 which would make our life easier to write code, see http://perldoc.perl.org/feature.html.

say "foo" instead of print "foo\n".
state $foo instead of having to use closures (my $foo; sub bar { $foo++ }).
given..when..default instead of if..elsif..elsif...else.
$foo = $bar // $baz instead of $foo = defined $bar ? $bar : $baz.
smart matching, see http://perldoc.perl.org/perlsyn.html#Smart-matching-in-detail

There are probably some other features which do not come to mind right now and which could be useful for Bugzilla. Maybe should we list them in this bug, and then we can decide if/when it worths the move to 5.10.1 (we should skip 5.10.0 as it had some major regressions).

I see nothing exciting in Perl 5.12 or Perl 5.14, so I doubt we would bump the min Perl version again in the near future.

summary: Offer Linux packagers an easy way to specify the location of the Bugzilla modules
description:
Created attachment 553979
fake Bugzilla.pm module for Linux packagers

In most Linux distributions, the Bugzilla modules (Bugzilla.pm and Bugzilla/*.pm) are not in the same directory as the *.cgi scripts when provided by a RPM or other package format. This forces them to edit all *.cgi scripts to fix the

  use lib qw(. lib);

line to make it point to the new location, e.g. /usr/share/bugzilla/lib.

The attached file is a fake Bugzilla.pm module which the packagers can put in the Perl directory, e.g. in /usr/lib/perl5/vendor_perl/5.x.y/ which will be loaded when the real Bugzilla.pm cannot be found. This module contains a $bz_root_dir variable which must point to the new location of the Bugzilla modules. With the example above, it would be:

  $bz_root_dir = '/usr/share/bugzilla/lib';

It will then add the new location in @INC and load the real Bugzilla.pm module transparently for the caller.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request:** Enhance Extensible Login System to Handle Intermediate Failure Points

**Description:**

The extensible login system currently only allows the bottom item in the stack to pass its failure code to the user. This limits the ability of intermediate items in the stack to indicate that a particular login method has failed, potentially leading to unexpected behavior and poor user experience.

To address this issue, it is proposed to modify the `get_login_info` function in `Bugzilla/Auth/Login/Stack.pm` to allow each item in the stack to return one of three possible outcomes:

1. **Success**: The item confirms that the login attempt was successful using its own method.
2. **Pass-through**: The item indicates that it cannot confirm the login, but another item in the stack may be able to succeed.
3. **Final failure**: The item indicates that the login has failed and no further attempts should be made.

By introducing this functionality, items in the stack will be able to provide more granular control over the login process, enabling better error handling and a more seamless user experience.

summary: All authenticated WebServices methods should require username/pass, token or a valid API key for authentication
description:
Bug 718319 and bug 725663 are perfect examples of how dangerous the web is. You can do remote JSON-RPC and XML-RPC calls using <form> HTML elements and using JavaScript to send data to a remote server, even if this server says it's not OK to use XmlHttpRequest remotely. We are currently relying on the Content-Type header to accept or reject calls, assuming the browser behaves accordingly to https://developer.mozilla.org/En/HTTP_access_control#Simple_requests, but we have no guarantee about that.

To protect critical WebServices methods such as those editing parameters, user accounts, or bugs, we should require a token for all methods which alter the DB. A token wouldn't be needed for read-only methods. This token would be returned by User.login, and would be valid for X minutes (we could make it valid till the caller calls User.logout, but I fear some callers would forget to log out). The token would of course be tied to the user ID, to avoid an attacker to use his own token with someone else credentials.

**Authentication Enhancement for WebServices Methods**

To enhance security and prevent unauthorized access to critical WebServices methods, we propose introducing authentication requirements for all editing operations. Specifically, we recommend that WebServices methods modifying database parameters, user accounts, or bugs should require one of the following:

* A valid username and password combination
* A token obtained through User.login, which would be tied to the user's ID and valid for a specified period (e.g., X minutes)
* A valid API key

This approach ensures that only authorized users can perform editing operations on our system. For read-only methods, no authentication will be required.

By implementing this enhancement, we aim to mitigate potential security vulnerabilities, such as those demonstrated in bugs 718319 and 725663, where malicious actors could exploit browser behavior to bypass expected security restrictions.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request Title:** Preserve User Session during Conflicting Changes in WebDAV-enabled ICS Files

**Description:**

The application should implement a mechanism to prevent the loss of user session data when encountering conflicting changes to an ICS file stored on a WebDAV server. When multiple users access and modify the same ICS file, the system currently closes the editing window and discards unsaved changes upon detecting conflicts with the latest version of the file.

**Key Requirements:**

* Implement a feature to retain the user's editing session despite conflicting changes.
* Provide an opportunity for the user to refresh or reload the remote calendar and resubmit their changes after resolving the conflict.

**Expected Behavior:**

When a user attempts to save changes to a WebDAV-enabled ICS file, but encounters conflicts with the latest version of the file, the application should:

1. Prevent the loss of unsaved changes.
2. Prompt the user to reload or refresh the remote calendar and resubmit their changes.

This enhancement aims to improve the overall user experience by minimizing data loss and providing a more seamless editing process when working with shared ICS files on WebDAV servers.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Enhancement Request:** Simplify Time Zone Management and Display in Lightning/Sunbird

The current user interface for managing time zones in Lightning/Sunbird is cumbersome and lacks essential features. Specifically, the list of available time zones is not sorted by GMT, and individual items do not display their corresponding GMT offset. 2.  **GMT Display:** Include explicit display of the timezone for each event, both when creating and viewing events.
3.  **Automatic OS Timezone Integration:** Integrate Lightning/Sunbird's timezone setting with the operating system's timezone, eliminating the need to manually update both settings upon changing locations.

Optional Enhancements:

1.  **Favorite Timezones:** Implement a feature allowing users to store frequently used time zones for quick access.
2.  **Quick Time Zone Switching:** Provide an option to change the timezone without navigating through preferences, improving user convenience.

These enhancements aim to streamline the process of managing time zones in Lightning/Sunbird, making it more user-friendly and efficient, particularly for frequent travelers or users accustomed to easy timezone management in other applications.

**Enhancement Request: Flexible Scheduling for Repeating Events/Tasks**

The current scheduling functionality in Lightning does not adequately support repeating events/tasks on specific days of a specific week. Specifically, users should be able to block out time on the 3rd Friday of every month without relying on a manual calculation or incorrect assumptions.

When attempting to schedule an event/task that repeats weekly with a specified interval (e.g., every 4 weeks), the system incorrectly schedules the events in months with 5 weeks. This is due to the current implementation's inability to account for variable week lengths within a month.

**Key Requirements:**

1. Allow users to schedule repeating events/tasks using a specific day of the week (e.g., Friday) and interval (e.g., every 4 weeks).
2. Ensure accurate scheduling regardless of the number of weeks in a month.
3. Provide flexibility for users to set custom start dates and recurrence patterns, including handling months with varying week lengths.

**Reproducible:** This issue is consistently observed when attempting to schedule repeating events/tasks exceeding 12 months with specific day and interval settings.

By implementing this enhancement, users will be able to efficiently schedule recurring events/tasks while accounting for the complexities of variable month lengths.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Error Reporting Enhancement Request**

The current CalDAV error reporting mechanism lacks sufficient information for users to understand the cause of errors. Specifically, the "Description" field in MODIFICATION_FAILED error messages is empty, making it difficult for users to diagnose issues.

	+ 403: "Forbidden"
	+ 404: "Not Found"

**Issue:** Inconsistent Behavior for Today Pane Minimization and Maximization

**Description:**

When using the F11 key or clicking on the Today Pane button to toggle its visibility, there exists inconsistent behavior regarding minimization and maximization states. Specifically:

* Hiding the Today Pane via F11 toggles its status between hidden (with a red cross in the corner) and minimized (but only visible by re-clicking the same button).
* Minimizing the Today Pane using the long bar with dots and arrows results in it being stuck in a minimized state, which cannot be maximized without re-clicking the same bar.

The current behavior leads to confusion regarding the two distinct states of visibility (hidden and minimized). To resolve this issue, we propose two potential solutions:

1. **Toggle between hidden and visible**: Always toggle the Today Pane's visibility between hidden and fully visible when using F11 or clicking on the Today Pane button.
2. **State-dependent behavior**: When pressing F11 or clicking on the Today Pane button, check if the pane is currently minimized. If it is, change its state to maximized.

**Reproducibility:** This issue can be consistently reproduced by following these steps:

1. Minimize the Today Pane using the long bar with dots and arrows.
2. Attempt to maximize the Today Pane using F11 or the Today Pane button in the right corner.
3. Observe that the pane remains minimized, unable to be maximized through these methods.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the enhancement request's main purpose and details:

**Issue:** Insufficient Vertical Space in Task Description Field at 600px Resolution

**Description:**

When working on a task with a vertical resolution of 600 pixels, particularly on Asus Eee PC models with a maximum resolution of 1024x600, the "Attachments" field occupies an excessive amount of space, leaving insufficient room for the "Description" field. This makes it challenging to read and write in the Description field.

**Expected Behavior:**

The description field should maintain at least two lines of vertical space to ensure readability and usability, regardless of the number of attachments added.

**Possible Solutions:**

1. **Dynamic Height Adjustment:** Adjust the height of the "Attachments" field based on the number of links attached, ensuring that it does not exceed three lines.
2. **Movable Line Separator:** Implement a movable line separator between the Description and Attachments fields, allowing users to customize the display layout as needed.
3. **Icon-Based Repeat and Reminder Fields:** Convert Repeat and Reminder fields into icons when they are less frequently used, freeing up space for other fields.

**Additional Feedback:**

* Clarify the distinction between "Icons" and "Icons and Text" modes in the task toolbar customization options to ensure users understand how small icons are displayed.
* Consider simplifying field separators by removing unnecessary vertical divisions, potentially reducing visual clutter and increasing usable space.

summary: Hide FlashBlock placeholder for blocked ads
description:
Created attachment 268638
Patch to remove Flashblock placeholder for most common Flash ads

This is a feature request to hide the FlashBlock placeholder for ads.  As discussed on the forums, it can be awkward to see a FlashBlock placeholder disappear when clicked.  The ad blocking mechanism is hiding the Flash ad, but not the placeholder.

http://forums.mozillazine.org/viewtopic.php?p=2801735

There are a couple of solutions, one being to change the FlashBlock code to recognize when an <embed> or <object> tag is hidden by the ad block code and then disable the placeholder.  But I'd rather not have the FlashBlock team change their code just to accommodate Camino, mostly because any time we make a change, we'll have to make sure they change their code as well.

So I think we should change our ad blocking CSS style to hide the Flashblock placeholder.  Since we aren't sure the order that a placeholder gets created and an ad gets hidden (at least I think we aren't sure), we'll need to modify ad_blocking.css to hide the placeholder whether the ad is visible or not (another reason not to modify the flashblock code since it may run before the ad is actually hidden).

For the most common Flash ads that I've seen, there is a tag structure like:
 <object>
  <embed src="some ad URL">
  </embed>
 </object>

Camino hides the <embed> tag, but usually the FlashBlock placeholder replaces the <object> tag with a <div> tag.  Argh, that means we can't use sibling selectors in the CSS.  Luckily, in this case the FlashBlock <div> tag will have an attribute embedsrc="some ad URL".  We can then add tags such as this to the ad_blocking.css code:

div[embedsrc*="/ad."]

In other words, copy the embed entries in ad_blocking.css and search-and-replace:
 :s/^embed.*\[src/div[embedsrc/

This hides the FlashBlock placeholder for the ads I've tested so far.  If there are still some that aren't hidden, we can figure out why not later.  

I'm adding a patch for all of the current entries in the CSS.  In the future, anytime you add an "embed" entry to ad_blocking.css, make sure to add a corresponding "div[embedsrc]" entry.  Or maybe there is a better solution?

**Request:** Enhance Ad Blocking by Hiding FlashBlock Placeholders for Blocked Ads

**Description:** Update the ad blocking CSS style to automatically hide FlashBlock placeholders for common Flash ads. This will ensure a seamless user experience when clicking on blocked ads, which are currently being replaced with a placeholder despite being hidden.

summary: Drag-and-dropping multiple URLs should open them in tabs of a single window
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; U; Intel Mac OS X; en) AppleWebKit/523.12.1 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/3.0.4 Safari/523.12.2
Build Identifier: Version 2007112812 (1.5.4)

Currently, when user drops multiple URLs (e.g., .webloc files from the Finder) on Camino icon, each URL is opened in a separate window. It is more convenient to have them opened in tabs of a single new window.

When the user opens multiple URLs, they are usually 1) related to each other in some context and 2) processed one-by-one. Single window with multiple tabs is better for this scenario. Multiple URLs are usually drag-and-dropped by those who prefer to use their own folder structures instead of the built-in bookmark functionality for the added flexibility. For example, such folders may have images, PDF files, text files and links (.webloc files) and usually correspond to some sort of a project. Bookmark folders do not have such flexibility. It is more convenient to open files in such folders in multiple tabs of a single window to retain the context and avoid mixing these windows with others that might be opened at the same time (mail, various reading etc.). Currently, to obtain this behavior, the user has to drag the first link, then open new tab, then navigate back to the folder that is now hidden by the browser window, drag the second link to Camino icon, repeat the process again. As an added complexity, the user has to keep track of what links she has already opened. It is much more convenient to pick-and-choose necessary link files using Command modifier in the Finder window, and then drag this selection to Camino as one transaction. Finally, it is much easier to close these links, as the user closes just one window, so it's easier to "rollback" opening multiple links.

For the less common scenario of comparing two windows side-by-side, the user will still be able to drag-and-drop these URLs separately to have them opened in separate windows. There's no need (and the screen estate) to compare 10 URLs side-by-side, so it's usually 2 or 3 windows, and they need to be re-positioned to not overlap, so there are lots of mouse movements anyway. Drag-and-dropping one-by-one is acceptable in this scenario.

I think that proposed behavior is superior in most situations and SHOULD be the default. However, in the single-window mode of operation (where all new pages open in new tabs), such behavior is expected and MUST be the default.

Reproducible: Always

summary: Default Home Page should be blank

Currently Camino uses http://www.mozilla.org/projects/camino/homepage.html as its default home page, which redirects to http://caminobrowser.org/start/, which contains a link to the http://caminobrowser.org/ and a Google search field. There's already a Google search field in the top right corner of the browser window, and the website for Camino is easily accessed via Help > Camino Home Page. Why the need for this home page? It is completely redundant and it is even abusing the user, because each time she opens a new window, she has to wait for this page to load. Most users change the home page to blank or to some other page, so the default value should be blank.

The whole 'home page' thing started because browser vendors wanted to maximize user visits to their 'portal' web sites so they could profit from advertising. The times have changed. Now, there's no need for default home page, it's time to make it blank. (On a side note, this might mark the end of the Home Page as people will start using bookmark bar or auto-complete for frequently-visited locations.)

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Implement Confirmation Option for File Downloads

**Description:**
We are requesting the addition of a preference to Camino that prompts users for confirmation when initiating a file download. This feature would provide an extra layer of security and convenience, allowing users to review and approve or cancel downloads before they begin.

**Justification:**
The current behavior, where files are downloaded immediately upon clicking a link, can lead to unintended consequences, such as accidental downloads requiring manual cleanup. By implementing a confirmation prompt, we aim to prevent these issues and provide a more user-friendly experience.

**Implementation Suggestions:**

1. Add a preference to prompt for confirmation when downloading a file.
2. Introduce an "Always Prompt" option for specifying the download folder, allowing users to choose whether to be prompted for each download location or always save files in the default location.

**Security Consideration:**
The absence of this feature may leave Camino vulnerable to security exploits, such as the "carpet bombing" issue affecting Safari. By implementing a confirmation prompt, we can mitigate potential risks and enhance user trust in the browser.

description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 6.1; WOW64; rv:5.0) Gecko/20100101 Firefox/5.0
Build Identifier: 

The new smartcache design defaults to a 1GB cache on large hdds resulting in up to 100,000 tiny files being created across a massive subdirectory tree. Mechanical HDD's cannot write(including deletion) many small files at once without flooding the hdd IO and causing thrashing which is what occurs when you clear a full cache (60,000+ files)

The new design would be suitable for a SSD but is fragmentation and thrashing hell on a mechanical hard drive.

Windows itself is castrated to a several hundred file delete rate per second for many small byte sized files usually maxing out a core while attempting to delete so many files. and when clearing the cache from within firefox it locks up the entire interface until the purge completes

Further, much of the content within the cache is under a KB. this in itself is a problem because you're using a 4K(as is the ntfs default on windows atleast) cluster for every single file under 4K which adds to fragmentation and a massive increase of the On Disk size of the files, Firefox's cache caps to the actual size limit but the On Disk size displays that up to 1.7x as much HDD space is actually in use.

Firefox should adapt an archive or image based cache that works similar to a virtual drive image, the thrashing would only occur when the cache file is first created, cache fragmentation would be eradicated similar to how a min/max identical page file remains unfragmented.

Reproducible: Always

standard:
Here's a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Optimize HTTP Cache Management for Mechanical Hard Drives

**Description:** The current smartcache design creates an excessive number of small files in the cache directory, leading to poor performance and increased fragmentation on mechanical hard drives. This results in slow write operations, thrashing, and system lock-ups during cache clearing.

**Impact:**

* Intensive disk I/O activity causes HDD thrashing and flooding
* Windows' file deletion rate is severely limited due to large numbers of small files
* Cache size is inflated due to inefficient storage allocation for small files (under 4KB)
* Fragmentation increases On Disk size, causing unnecessary space consumption

**Proposed Solution:** Implement an archive or image-based cache mechanism similar to a virtual drive image. This would reduce fragmentation and eliminate thrashing, with minimal impact on system performance. The solution should be designed to minimize the initial creation of the cache file, ensuring efficient storage allocation and reduced On Disk size.

**Scope:** This enhancement is essential for improving caching performance on mechanical hard drives, ensuring user-friendly interface behavior during cache clearing, and optimizing system resources.

summary: make filenames in @line comments work for runtime exceptions
description:
Created attachment 538983
my partial patch

The "atline" option (js -o atline or js -e 'options("atline")' -f) enables parsing of comments in the form:

 //@line 20 "foo.js"

And these comments are used to alter the line number and filename of error reports. Apparently on the line number portion of the comments are documented.  

Specifying a filename in an @line comment works for compilation errors, but not for runtime errors.  If you use an @line comment with a filename specified, any runtime errors will be reported as if they occured in the file specified by the last @line comment.

I'd like to fix this and make @line comments work for runtime errors.  My use case is that I've got thousands of lines of code that need to be inside of a single closure function.  But I want to break those lines of code down into separate files for ease of management.  I use a Makefile to automatically concatenate the files and add the function wrapper that makes them part of the same closure.  But then for debugging, all errors get reported against the one big file rather than against the individual files.  Not a hugely compelling use-case, but it seemed like something fun for me to tackle as my first foray into SpiderMonkey internals.

Currently jsscan.cpp does not retain the contents of the @line comments. That is pretty easy to fix.  One approach I tried was to define an AtLine struct to hold the data from each @line comment, and then create a JSCList of AtLines and store it in the TokenStream.  My problem with that approach is getting the data out of the TokenStream when I need it.  By the time a runtime error occurs, the TokenStream with its list of AtLine stucts is long gone.

I was able to use the atline data in jsscript.cpp when creating a Script object.  That means that code inside functions thinks it is in the file named by //@line comment nearest to the start of the function.  It doesn't work for top-level code though, and it doesn't work for functions that are broken across files.

I thought about copying all the AtLine data to the JSContext or something, but can't figure out the memory management issues.

A second approach I've tried is to append atline data to the primary filename.  So suppose the file foo.js looks like this:

foo()
//@line 1 "bar.js"
bar()
//@line 1 "baz.js"

In jsscan.cpp, I'd change the TokenStream.filename to:

  foo.js\n\t2=1:bar.js\n\t4=1:baz.js

The newlines and tabs make this an illegal filename, but make it print nicely if it is ever displayed raw.  This filename gets stored like a regular filename and is accessible when a runtime error occurs, and is properly memory managed, like a regular filename.  

This store the atline data in the filename is kind of kudgy, but also seems like the most straightforward way to approch the problem.  My problem now is to figure out when to extract the atline data from the filename.  I've modified js_ErrorToException in jsexn.cpp to extract the correct filename and line number, but it turns out that this only sets the lineNumber and fileName property of the Error object, not the file and line that are printed by default, and not the stack trace.  I think I just don't understand the SpiderMonkey error reporting infrastructure well enough.

I'll attach my current code, using the one-big-filename approach. I'd be happy to attach my linked-list-of-AtLine-structs attempt, too, if anyone is interested. 

This is my first attempt at a SpiderMonkey patch, and my C is rusty and my C++ is pretty non-existant, so go easy on me...

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Title:** Enhance @line Comment Support for Runtime Exceptions

**Description:**

The `@line` comment feature in SpiderMonkey allows for customization of error reporting by specifying line numbers and filenames. Currently, this functionality only works for compilation errors, but not runtime exceptions. This enhancement aims to extend the support of `@line` comments to runtime errors.

**Use Case:**

In a specific development scenario where thousands of lines of code are wrapped in a single closure function, it is desirable to break these lines down into separate files for easier management. However, when debugging, all errors get reported against the single big file rather than individual files.

**Implementation:**

The enhancement involves storing `@line` comment data in the TokenStream and making it accessible during runtime error reporting. Two alternative approaches have been explored:

1. Storing `AtLine` structs in a JSCList within the TokenStream.
2. Appending atline data to the primary filename, which is then stored and accessed when a runtime error occurs.

**Current Status:**

A partial patch has been created, implementing the second approach. However, there are outstanding issues related to extracting atline data from the filename during runtime error reporting.

**Request:**

To complete this enhancement, it would be beneficial to:

1. Resolve memory management concerns for storing `AtLine` structs in a JSContext.
2. Finalize the extraction of atline data from the filename during runtime error reporting, ensuring proper integration with SpiderMonkey's error reporting infrastructure.

Two more fonts to consider for the fallback list:

1) Microsoft Sans Serif -- This is the default font used for form controls (it's what MS Shell Dlg maps to).  Since it is an adaptation of the old MS Sans Serif raster font, a GDI-style rendering is arguably closest to its "intended" appearance.  (And it looks better that way, too.)

Also, as a monospace font, the positioning fidelity of natural seems less relevant.

Propose adding Microsoft Sans Serif and Consolas to the list of typefaces that fall back to GDI classic rendering. This enhancement aims to improve the appearance and consistency of these fonts when rendered using GDI, which would align with their original design intent.

**Title:** Optimized Typed Array Creation and Access Performance

**Description:** This patch set enhances the performance of TypedArray creation and access by implementing several improvements.

The primary changes include:

* Eliminating the use of C++ objects in favor of inline slots within the JSObject, reducing creation time.
* Updates to the TypeScript (TM) and JavaScript (JM) compilers to generate optimized instructions for TypedArray operations.
* Fixing JM to correctly generate code for 'length' property access on TypedArray, resulting in faster access times.

Additionally, this patch set fixes uses of the API in Firefox and passes try server testing. The performance improvements are demonstrated through benchmark results, which show significant reductions in creation time and access speed compared to previous implementations.

**Key Performance Metrics:**

* Creation time has been reduced by up to 65% for large arrays.
* Access times have been improved by up to 83% for 'length' property access on TypedArray.
* Overall performance improvements are evident across various benchmark tests, including Bocoup and skinning benchmarks.

**System Requirements:** Tested on a Macintosh system with Intel Core i7 processor, 8GB RAM, and Darwin kernel version 10.7.4.

**Reproducibility:** Always reproducible.

summary: support @sourceURL=... comment annotation in JavaScript for eval, script injection, inline script blocks, etc
description:
I had a conversation with mrbkap and fitzgen about a very limited scope request, which is to bring in support for @sourceURL annotation in JavaScript code, similar to how Firebug currently supports for eval(), for all forms of JavaScript code parsing/execution, especially those which don't already have a good "label" (like what the source filename/URL is).

Firebug allows:

// @sourceURL=...

If you add that at the very end of a block of code that you pass to eval(), it will use the specified filename label for debugging and other output purposes, when referring to that script. This is quite useful for when you load a file via XHR, for instance, and either eval() it or pass it to script injection, by creating a script element and setting its .text property, etc.

Reference: http://blog.getfirebug.com/2009/08/11/give-your-eval-a-name-with-sourceurl/

My request is that the `JSScript::filename` property be overridable if such a comment annotation appears in JS code that is parsed/executed. In that way, this filename "label" will be available to tools like the debugger or the web console devtool, etc.

There is one case that mrbkap identified that needs special casing, which is that `chrome://global/...` URLs are given special permissions, so any annotation with that type of value should ignore that value and NOT set it, thus preventing scripts from artificially elevating their own privileges.

Also, I am aware that there's more comprehensive work being done on Source Mapping (I believe that's what fitzgen is working on), which as we discussed is not a superset of this request, but related yet orthagonal. The Source Mapping stuff is about taking a script and relating it back to a specific resource on a server (like a source file, etc), whereas this request is to give an arbitrary label (often a "filename") to a script container, for the purposes of the devtooling outputs, only. It would augment what the Source Mapping stuff will eventually provide.

For instance, you wouldn't necessarily map a little snippet of code that you want to eval() to a real resource on the server, but you might want to give it a label like "mouse-events.js" so that in debugging output, you knew what the snippet was.

Technically, @sourceURL is slightly misleading, since it's not really supposed to convey any semantics about the label being a URL, per se. @Label might be more accurate. However, I'm proposing that we do @sourceURL to maintain compatibility with how firebug's feature already works with eval() code.

This request will let our native devtools, like our debugger and web console, have the same functionality that firebug has currently hacked in with @sourceURL.

2. Visit page containing iframe from another domain, say outer.com/outer containing an iframe with the document inner.com/first. The inner.com/first document tried to set a cookie.

The rationale is that by interacting with the iframe, the user implicitely expressed a certain trust in that content. So it very likely isn't a tracking advertisement.

**Enhanced Error Reporting for PSM**

The current error reporting mechanism for Public Key Infrastructure (PSM) errors does not clearly indicate which certificate has been revoked when using strict OCSP mode. This can lead to confusion and difficulty in troubleshooting issues, particularly when classic verification methods succeed while libpkix verification encounters a "revoked certificate" error.

To improve diagnostic capabilities and facilitate the adoption of strict OCSP verification, we propose enhancing PSM error reporting to provide more detailed information about revoked certificates. Specifically, the system should identify which specific certificate has been revoked, enabling users to take corrective action and resolve issues more efficiently.

This enhancement will enable more accurate troubleshooting and promote the use of strict OCSP verification, ultimately improving overall security and reliability.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Implement High-Resolution Platform Timers for Windows

**Purpose:** Improve the accuracy and reliability of timers on the Windows platform by implementing high-resolution timing functionality.

**Details:**

The current QPC (Query Performance Counter) implementation has been identified as having issues with monotonicity, particularly across suspend/hibernate events. To address this, a new timer implementation is required that utilizes a self-correcting/calibration approach similar to PRMJ_Now, but without truncation and conversion to an actual date.

The proposed solution involves leveraging the multimedia timer, which provides monotonic behavior, and using it as a guide for clock-skew detection. Additionally, the calibration data could be shared with TimeStamp::Now to enhance consistency between different timing functions.

**Implementation:** The new timer implementation should be developed in a separate file, analogous to TimeStamp_posix.cpp, but specific to the Windows platform (e.g., TimeStamp_windows.cpp).

To inform this feature, we aim to develop algorithms for:

This enhancement has the potential to improve user experience by reducing perceived page load times and optimizing resource utilization.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request for Float Support in readPixels() Function**

Current WebGL implementation restricts the use of `readPixels()` function to retrieve pixel data from the framebuffer when using floating-point textures. While floating-point textures are supported via the "OES_texture_float" extension, attempting to read back pixels as floats results in an error.

**Request Details:**

* **Expected Behavior**: Allow `readPixels()` to return pixel data as float values.
* **Current Limitation**: Only unsigned byte (UNSIGNED_BYTE) types are supported for reading pixels from the framebuffer, while floating-point textures are available through the "OES_texture_float" extension.
* **Impact**: Ability to read back pixel data in its original float format would be desirable.

**Example Use Case:**

When attempting to use `readPixels()` with a floating-point texture, the following code results in an error:
```javascript
var pixels = new Float32Array(framebuffer.width * framebuffer.height * 4);
gl.readPixels(0, 0, framebuffer.width, framebuffer.height, gl.RGBA, gl.FLOAT, pixels);
```
Error message: "WebGL: ReadPixels: type: invalid enum value 0x1406"

This enhancement request seeks to modify the `readPixels()` function to support float values, enabling more precise and efficient handling of floating-point textures in WebGL applications.

summary: Extensions cannot find out when a certificate fails certificate chain validation
description: +++ This bug was initially created as a clone of Bug #686095 +++ +++ This bug was initially created as a clone of Bug #644640 +++ In bug 686095 comment 2, Peter Eckersley wrote: > One example of why we're tearing our hair out over this issue is that the href="https://trac.torproject.org/projects/tor/wiki/doc/HTTPSEverywhere/ > SSLObservatorySubmission">Decentralized SSL Observatory can't get copies > of invalid TLS certificates that are sent to the user's browser unless the > user clicks through the security dialog. What that means is that our > extension can't detect/study an attack like this one: In PSM, when we reject a certificate, we notify the callbacks for the socket via the nsIBadCertListener2 interface. I've been doing a number of things within the JS engine where I'm integrating with external libraries that want a per-process initialization. For example, opagent's op_open_agent() ends up creating a file named after the current pid.

As far as I can tell, there is no way to do this sort of module initialization safely from within the JS engine. You can't use a global lock because NSPR (and probably some underlying thread libraries) does not provide a static initializer, so the creation of the global lock itself races.

I think we should have a JS wrapper for the same functionality.

(I've been using a static initialization flag from within JS_NewRuntime, but there's no restriction as far as I know on a single runtime per process.)

**Issue Description:**

**Request for UI Message String Bundle Loading Optimization**

Current implementation loads UI message string bundles in `nsNSSComponent::Init()`, ensuring they are accessible on the main thread. However, this approach has limitations, as some components use these strings off-thread, leading to inefficiencies.

To address this, we propose two key improvements:

1. **Eliminate non-main-thread usage**: Remove all instances where string bundles are accessed from threads other than the main thread.

By implementing these changes, we aim to optimize the handling of UI message string bundles, enhancing the overall efficiency and reliability of our system.

summary: Server certificate is only trusted for a specific port after exception. Alternating certificates on one port creates constant exception prompts..
description:
I am developing web server software and testing it with firefox.
The server supports SSL with virtual servers. It supports dynamic reconfiguration including change of the server certificate. For testing purposes, I am using self-signed certificates.

There are several scenarios where the exception handling does not work as I would expect.

Here are the test cases :

1) I connect to  https://myserver.mydomain.com:port1 with Firefox
2) I receive cert1 which has the proper hostname in the subject
3) I accept the security exception.
4) I connect to https://myserver.mydomain.com:port2
5) I receive cert1 which has the proper hostname in the subject. I get another exception dialog, even though it was previously trusted. It seems to me that there should be a way to trust the certificate altogether, for all ports, and not for just one specific port. This is the first part of the problem.
The trust is specific to a particular URL, including protocol, port and hostname. It doesn't make sense to me. I should be able to trust the certificate according to what it says it's good for, ie. the content of its subject. Either I trust the certificate, or I don't. I believe this business of trusting a given certificate only for a particular URL violates PKIX specifications, such as RFC 5280.

I believe that when it comes to re-using the certificate for the same certificate for the same hostname on the same port, this restriction is seriously misguided. One should be able to do that without getting prompted again.

If the concern is that the certificate may contain multiple subjectAltNames for other hosts, or wildcards, perhaps Firefox could check for those during the exception confirmation process, and present the full list to the user, so that he can trust the cert or not. Anyway, IMO, those should always be displayed to the user.

6) I reconfigure the server at https://myserver.mydomain.com:port1 to use a new cert, cert2
7) I connect to  https://myserver.mydomain.com:port1 with Firefox again
8) I receive cert2 which has the proper hostname in the subject, but was not previously seen
9) I accept the security exception. So far, so good.
10) I reconfigure the server at https://myserver.mydomain.com:port1 to use the old cert, cert1
11) I connect to  https://myserver.mydomain.com:port1 with Firefox again
12) I receive cert1 which has the proper hostname in the subject
13) I receive another security exception dialog. This should not happen, because I already made an exception for this same URL and same certificate cert in step 3. But now, Firefox forgot this decision. Presumably, this exception was overwritten in step 9.
This is problem number 2.
This is not a theoretical problem. Server farms with load balancers do exist, which may end up presenting different certificates for each connection to the same URL, though real deployments would hopefully use proper certificates that chain to a trust anchor, so one would not expect exceptions to show up. However, it is impossible to test such scenarios with Firefox without a real CA.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request: Enhance Certificate Trusting Mechanism for Consistency and User Experience**

The current certificate trusting mechanism in Firefox exhibits inconsistent behavior when dealing with multiple certificates on the same hostname, protocol, and port. Specifically:

* When a user accepts an exception for a specific URL (protocol, port, and hostname), they are only trusted for that exact combination. This leads to repeated exception prompts when accessing different ports or reusing the same certificate on the same hostname.
* When a server dynamically reconfigures certificates, Firefox forgets previously accepted exceptions, resulting in unnecessary security dialogs.

To address these issues, we propose enhancing the trusting mechanism as follows:

1. Trusting a certificate should be based on its subject, rather than specific URL combinations (protocol, port, and hostname).
2. When reusing a certificate for the same hostname on the same port, Firefox should not prompt the user for another exception.
3. To alleviate concerns about certificates containing multiple subjectAltNames or wildcards, consider displaying the full list to the user during exception confirmation.

By implementing these enhancements, we aim to improve the user experience and ensure compliance with PKIX specifications (RFC 5280).

**Feature Request: JS Shell Compile Flag for Determinism**

A new JavaScript shell compile flag, `--enable-more-deterministic`, will be introduced to enhance the determinism of the JS shell. This flag will enable two key modifications:

The certificate validation configuration should be deferred until the first time certificate validation occurs, rather than being performed during startup. This involves re-arranging the initialization sequence to minimize code execution and page faults during startup.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Enable GSSAPI Interface Access from Extensions

**Description:**

The GSSAPI (Generic Security Services Application Program Interface) feature, which provides Single Sign-On (SSO) capabilities and enhances both security and usability, is not accessible to extensions in Thunderbird. This prevents users from utilizing SASL-GSSAPI with the MANAGESIEVE protocol provided by the "sieve" extension.

**Current Situation:**

While servers such as Dovecot, Exim4, OpenLDAP, and Jabberd2 support SASL-GSSAPI, GUI clients like Thunderbird have not fully implemented this feature. Specifically, the MANAGESIEVE protocol's current implementation in Thunderbird does not allow access to GSSAPI features.

**Expected Outcome:**

To enable SSO capabilities for users, it is necessary to either:

1. Implement native support for the MANAGESIEVE client within Thunderbird.
2. Make the GSSAPI interface accessible from extensions, allowing developers to create custom solutions using JavaScript and C-Types.

This enhancement request aims to facilitate seamless integration of SASL-GSSAPI with the MANAGESIEVE protocol in Thunderbird, promoting improved security and usability for users.

The current implementation fails to directly convert an `ArrayBufferView` to an array when using the `nsIDOMParser.parseFromBuffer` method. This results in an error due to the inability to convert a JavaScript object into an array.

summary: Add an optional message argument to MOZ_ASSERT
description:
Created attachment 586598
Patch with a few two-argument users

Often the message argument to NS_ABORT_IF_FALSE is unhelpful (think non-null argument assertions).  But sometimes it's useful, for assertions which are non-obviously correct or which are particularly complex.  Variadic macros allow us to add an optional message to MOZ_ASSERT assertions.  Sentiment on IRC and elsewhere wasn't opposed to adding an optional message (although it was adamantly opposed to requiring a message :-) ).

MSVC 2005 (the oldest we care about) supports variadic macros, and gcc's supported them much longer, so I think we have the compiler support.  There's at least one unconditional use of variadic macros in the tree, so theoretically any compiler that doesn't support them is broken already.  But it can't hurt to be cautious, so let's start small.  This patch makes MOZ_ASSERT take either one or two arguments and changes one file to use the two-argument form (that clearly wanted it) to ensure it works.  We can let this sit for awhile, then go about announcing the change more broadly once nobody's complained, and making the other assertion macros take an optional message too.

I asked Jesse about his preferred message format, since he's probably the biggest consumer of the current assertion message syntax, and he suggested this.  This also happens to fit in the previous syntax, so it should be even more compatible.  We're not sure what sort of message length will end up being used in practice, so we're going to play the exact format by ear.  (Embedding the message this way might mean the typical fuzzbug that copies the assert into the summary might go past normal length limits, in theory.  Whether this will happen, we'll only find out with greater use of it.)

summary: Allow chrome and content to run on different threads
description:
After going through bug 384412 and having some extended discussions with luke, I've been looking for a somewhat minimal extension to the event/threads model which avoids locking the browser on content stalls.  For now this is an experimental bug to help me learn some of our events/threads/etc. code and see if I can prototype these changes.

Definition: a |constellation| is either all of chrome or a collection of content data (JS compartments, windows/tabs) that is disconnected from all other content constellations.

Use a pool of threads with a single, shared event queue (as now).  As new events come in, threads may pick them up and start executing, under the following constraints:

1. All events start out in chrome, and may switch among constellations as they execute.

2. Constellations may be locked exclusively.  A thread must lock a constellation in order to access any of its data, and will generally hold the lock until switching to another constellation.  There is no multithreaded access to any data.

3. Chrome is locked only when in active use by a thread, and is unlocked as the thread tries to enter content.  Additionally, once a thread starts executing a content script, it holds the lock on that content constellation until the event finishes.  This is only done for the first such content constellation, to keep weird addons from deadlocking, and otherwise ensures run-to-completion for content.

The main idea here is that even if content is stalled, it will not keep chrome locked and chrome scripts can continue to execute.  Even if those chrome scripts block when trying to enter the stalled content, their threads will unlock chrome first and other threads can then start executing other pending events.

Now, a few problems:

4. If many events require access to content, all threads in the pool could end up blocked trying to enter the content.

5. This seems to really break run-to-completion for chrome, with unknown effects on the browser and addons.

So, a refinement:

6. Only keep two threads in the pool, a main thread and a reserve thread.  Normally, only the main thread runs, and behaves as it does now (since it is the only running thread, there is no lock contention).

7. When a "high priority" UI input event comes in (e.g. a mouse click) activate a watchdog and if small X ms pass without the event being serviced, give the event to the reserve thread.  The reserve thread starts executing (ignoring events further up in the queue), running chrome handlers and scheduling another event to call any content handlers once content wakes back up.  The reserve thread should avoid touching content, though an addon could break this --- the reserve thread would then block, oh well.

Points 1-3 do not require a notion of a high priority event and are cleaner, but due to 4. would really need per-constellation event queues to scale well.  But doing that is more complicated, and due to 5. may not work well in practice, so going with 6. and 7. for experimenting, even if that is not the permanent solution, seems a good way to go.

Here is a rewritten description of the enhancement request in standardized, professional language:

**Enhancement Request: Asynchronous Execution of Chrome and Content**

The current event/threads model locks the browser on content stalls, preventing chrome scripts from executing. To address this issue, we propose an extension to the event/threads model that allows chrome and content to run on different threads.

**Key Concepts:**

* A **constellation** represents either all chrome processes or a collection of disconnected content data (JS compartments, windows/tabs).
* A pool of threads with a shared event queue is used for execution.
* Events start in chrome and may switch among constellations as they execute.
* Constellations can be locked exclusively to prevent multithreaded access.

**Goal:**

The goal is to enable chrome scripts to continue executing even if content is stalled, without blocking the browser. This is achieved by introducing a refinement that limits the number of threads in the pool to two (main and reserve) and triggers the reserve thread to run high-priority events when the main thread is blocked.

**Key Features:**

* The main thread runs as usual, with no lock contention.
