this is a result of a discussion on the mail-news mailing list.  I wrote:
"""
as irritating as this may be to some folks, after many years of being a rabid
bottom poster I'm starting to see the value of top posting.  its nonintuitive
but I believe it's better human factors given the low usability of current
e-mail clients.  You can see the response right away without doing anything you
can quickly evaluate the message as to whether or not you want to look further,
you can quickly find the latest changes.  What's not to like?  (Yes, I know lots

on the space bar a half a dozen or more times just to get to the latest
commentary, having no way to go backwards (apparently) other than scrolling with
a mouse is really ugly if your hands don't work right.

(note: by update, I mean the text contributed by the message sender. for example
in this message the first update would start out with "as irritating as")

update would be a huge improvement.  Being able to jump to the next update would
be wonderful.  Not automatically jumping off of the end of the message to the
next message would be heavenly.  Making all of these capabilities keystroke
bound so that those of us using speech recognition can just dictate commands
would earn significant gratitude.

people use top posting because it fits their cognitive processes better.  Fix

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request Title:** Enhance Statusbar/Save-to Dialog to Prevent Malicious Email Infection

**Description:**

The statusbar and save-to dialog should be modified to prevent potential virus infections from malicious emails. Currently, certain types of emails can display lengthy links that appear harmless at first glance, but contain embedded objects or viruses. To mitigate this risk, the following enhancements are recommended:

1. **Shorten displayed links**: Limit the length of displayed links in the statusbar and save-to dialog to prevent users from accessing potentially malicious links.
2. **Warning notifications**: Introduce a warning notification when a user attempts to access an embedded object via a hyperlink, indicating that this is an unusual behavior for normal emails.

By implementing these enhancements, we can improve the security of our application and protect users from potential virus infections through malicious email attachments.

**Request Description:**

Improve Mail & Newsgroup Account Settings for Multiple SMTP Servers

The current implementation only allows configuring a single SMTP server in the Server Settings > Advanced > SMTP tab. This limitation causes issues when sending emails, as it prevents the use of available alternative servers if the primary one is unreachable.

**Functional Enhancement Request:**

Allow specifying a prioritized list of multiple SMTP servers for each account, enabling the system to automatically select and use the first available server in case the primary one is inaccessible. This feature should be applied consistently across all account configurations, including those set to default outgoing SMTP servers.

**Rationale:**

This functionality has been previously requested and acknowledged by the development team but remains unresolved. Implementing this enhancement will improve email sending reliability and user experience by enabling seamless fallback to available alternative SMTP servers in case of primary server unreachability.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Enhancement Request:**

Implement an nsICategoryManager-based plugin manager in Mozilla 1.8, leveraging existing backend functionality.

**Description:**

The current Firefox plugin manager will be replaced with a new implementation based on nsICategoryManager. This will involve modifying the following files:

* `browser.js`
* `plugins.js` (in the prefwindow content directory)
* `plugins.xul`

The addition of this feature is expected to enhance user experience by providing an efficient and effective plugin management system.

**Additional Requirements:**

1. The code for reading the "browser.download.pluginOverrideTypes" property will be integrated into the main mail/news file (`msgMail3PaneWindow.js`) to accommodate scenarios where the user launches Mozilla in mail/news mode.

3. A suitable placement will be identified within the Mozilla configuration system for the button opening the plugin manager window.

**Known Issues:**

1. The "browser.download.pluginOverrideTypesNotHandled" property requires further investigation due to its current limitation of not functioning correctly when multiple browser windows are open.
2. Two potential solutions exist:
	* Ensure that the code reading the "pluginOverrideTypes"-property is only executed once per session, possibly by adding a note in the hidden DOM window.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request for Enhancement (RFE)**

**Feature Description:** Create Symlink Support within Bookmarks

The feature proposal involves allowing users to create symbolic links between bookmarks. This enables the creation of bidirectional relationships between folders, where changes made to one folder's contents are automatically reflected in its corresponding linked folder.

**Example Scenario:**

A user has two top-level bookmark folders: "Linux" and "Programming". They want to establish a reciprocal relationship between these folders by creating symbolic links within them. For instance, "Programming->Linux" would link to the same content as "Linux->Programming", ensuring that updates made in one folder are mirrored in the other.

**Objective:** This feature enhancement aims to provide users with greater flexibility and efficiency in managing their bookmarks by allowing the creation of symbolic links between folders.

description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.7.5) Gecko/20041217 MultiZilla/1.6.4.0b
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.0; en-US; rv:1.7.5) Gecko/20041217 MultiZilla/1.6.4.0b

This is about lossages due to the way mozilla stores mail.  Related bugs are
103993, 116443, 247223, and no doubt others I haven't bothered to look for.

All these bugs are related to needs to change the mail format.  My goal in
adding yet another bug is to implore y'all to try to consider all the issues
together in devising another format.  That's why I'm not just adding this to
just ONE of these other bugs.

Some points:

Backups (meaning e.g., tape backups of all files, not just in mozilla)
------- 

Using the current format (which I guess is unix inbox format), whenever a
message is added to any mail file (i.e. "folder"), such as inbox or sent or
whatever, that file then needs to be backed up at some point.  My mail files
tend to be huge, what with all the attachments.  This means that every time I
get an new email message, the next incremental backup has to once again back
up a 1GB file, even though only 1KB changed in that file.  This is bad.
Using finer granularity of files internally would solve this.

Human readability
-----------------

Most likely, some solution, following others in the past, will be something
like one message per file, or maybe one thread per file.  (Though I can
imagine other choices, such as using diff-based version control.)  PLEASE
make sure these files have the following features:

1. A humble human such as myself can read and edit them with a plain file
   editor without breaking anything.  (This seems to be a design feature of
   the current system, although the system for checking whether an index file
   is still valid for the mail file it is supposed to be indexing seems to
   leave something to be desired.)  This is very useful when something else
   has been entirely too clever.

2. A humble human such as myself can look at the directory structure without
   any special tools and have a prayer of guessing which file contains what
   messages.  E.g., the filename might include the timestamp of the message.

3. They are not locked against being copied, viewed, or backed up by normal
   user mode programs.  In particular, this implies:

4. Resist the temptation to embed the mail into some database file.  While
   this allows clever searching, it makes the file opaque to normal humans,
   and usually makes copying or backing up the file a nightmare.

Merging and syncing
-------------------

I would really like to be able to merge (mail-diff?) different mail files.
In the worst case, this can be done with diff (or its ilk) using the current
inbox format.  Please keep this in mind when designing a new format, so that
it is easy to make tools to do mergin.  E.g., if each message is a file, then
a diff on the directory should give most of what you need to merge.  (This
relates to my point (2) above.)

Reproducible: Always

Here's a standardized description that conveys the main purpose and details of the enhancement request in clear, concise language:

**Enhancement Request: Improved Mail Format for Better Performance, Usability, and Backup Efficiency**

The current mail format used by Mozilla has several limitations, resulting in significant performance issues, backup inefficiencies, and difficulties with merging and syncing mail data. This enhancement request proposes a new mail format that addresses these concerns.

**Key Requirements:**

1. **Improved Backup Efficiency**: The new format should allow for finer granularity of files internally, enabling incremental backups only for modified sections rather than entire files.
2. **Human-Readable Files**: Mail files should be designed to be easily readable and editable with plain file editors, without breaking any functionality. This includes features such as:
	* Timestamp-based filenames
	* Clear directory structure
	* No locking against normal user mode programs (e.g., copying, viewing, or backing up)
3. **Merging and Syncing**: The new format should facilitate easy merging of different mail files, potentially using diff tools to identify changes.
4. **Database-Free Design**: Avoid embedding mail data in database files, which can make the file opaque to normal users and hinder backup processes.

**Impact:**

Implementing a new mail format that addresses these concerns will improve overall performance, reduce backup times, and enhance user productivity. The proposed design should prioritize human readability, flexibility, and compatibility with various tools and workflows.

**Reproducibility:** This issue is consistently reproducible across all environments.

list is set to threaded, and all the threads are collapsed, the only indicating
you have that a new message for a thread is a small green downward-pointing

some cases, I've had hundreds of threads in a list, and a message for a
three-week old thread would appear, and it takes me a long time to find that thread.

The work-around I use is to sort by date, click on the message, and then sort by
thread again.  I would prefer not to have to use this work-around.

We propose implementing two new features in the Thunderbird email client to enhance user experience.

**Request:** Implement Toggleable Sticky Search Feature for Message Pane

**Purpose:** Provide users with the ability to control the behavior of the sticky search feature in the message pane, allowing them to switch between applying and clearing the search term when changing folders.

**Request for Inline Image Display Enhancement**

We propose modifying the application's behavior when viewing email attachments with images. Currently, only images with a specific content disposition type ("inline") are displayed inline within the email body. We would like to enable the display of all attached images in-line, regardless of their content disposition type.

**Key Requirements:**

1. Display all attached images in-line within the email body.
2. Maintain the current behavior for images with "inline" content disposition type.

	* Never: Always display attachments as icons.
	* Inlined: Display attachments inline, but respect content disposition type.
	* Always: Force all attachments to be displayed inline.

**Expected Behavior:**

This enhancement would improve user experience by ensuring that forwarding messages is done effectively and efficiently, without introducing unnecessary notifications or complications.

summary: Account Wizard: Parallelize the guessConfig() heuristic
description:
When we failed all other methods and start checking common mail server hostnames and ports, we currently do that sequentially, one hostname/port at a time (albeit incoming and outgoing in parallel, I think). The whole process takes a lot of time, often between 30s and 3 minutes - if you do it the first time, second time for the same domain is faster. The latter suggests that a lot of the time is spent with DNS lookups. The rest of the time is probably TCP handshakes - they are low bandwidth, high latency.

I think we should save a *lot* of time, with only little waste of resources, if we did all the attempts in parallel. I.e. we start trying to connect to imap.example.com:995, imap.example.com:143, pop.example.com:993, pop.example.com:143, pop3.example.com:143 etc. all at the same time.

We record the results in an internal data structure, and at the end compare and return the best result. As optimization, we may decide to abort the search once we get a success on a host/port and all higher-preference host/ports already failed (are no longer outstanding), to avoid a full search when a high-preference like imap.example.com:995 succeeds.

**Request:** Enhance Account Wizard Configuration Process

**Description:** Improve the efficiency of the `guessConfig()` heuristic by parallelizing the process of checking common mail server hostnames and ports. summary: Thunderbird doesn't use POP3 pipelining
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux x86_64; en-US; rv:1.9.1.8) Gecko/20100214 Ubuntu/9.10 (karmic) Firefox/3.5.8
Build Identifier: 

Current (3.0.3) Thunderbird doesn't use pipelining when doing POP3, even if the server advertize it.

This is a huge performance hit when dealing with many small messages, for instance, because the roundtrip time slows progress a lot.

For instance. you download a message (RETR) and then you delete it (DELE) before retrieving the second message. If your RTT is 100ms, your maximum download speed is 5 messages per second (retr+dele), independiently of your bandwidth.

If you piggyback the "dele" in the next "retr", your download speed would go to 10msgs/s, a big improvement.

If thunderbird knows which messages it want to download, it can do multiple "retr" in advance (backlog), to keep the line busy for the next, let say, 2 seconds, and insert "dele" in the stream, as needed. This way the message downloading could fully use your download bandwidth. You are not limited for RTT.

As thunderbird is now, leaving messages in the server doubles your download speed, because you don't do the "dele" step. Piggybacking the "dele" on the next command would double download speed, the same that leaving messages on server.

This would be a trivial code change, but a huge performance booster, even limited by RTT.

Improving the intelligence in TB to fully use the download bandwidth via command pipeling would be amazing. The main point would be how much "retr" commands would be in the pipeline, and this value should take acount of bandwidth and RTT. This can be matematically modeled.


Reproducible: Always

summary: Consider DNS MX in autoconfig
description:
When we try to find a configuration for an email address, we currently only look at the domain in the email address.
This won't work for domain hosters which host many customer domains and do not publish the config themselves (see bug 534722).
For those, we are likely to find a config, if we query based on the domain the DNS MX record (the server which receives mail for that domain). Due to SSL limitations, it typically has the hostname in the domain of the hoster, not the customer.

So,
If all lookups apart from the heuristic failed,
1. look up DNS MX <domain-in-emailaddress>, get e.g. mx1.dreamhost.com
2. take the SLD only, e.g. dreamhost.com
   (attention for .co.uk - Mozilla/Firefox has a list of those)
3. start the lookup again from the beginning, for that new domain,
   including ISP fetch, Mozilla DB.
4. I'm not sure whether we should start the heuristic on the original domain or the MX domain, or both. In favor of a faster probe and/or limiting the amount of connections, we should be careful before doing both.

**Enhancement Request: Enhanced Autoconfig Lookup for Domain Hosters**

The autoconfig lookup mechanism currently relies solely on the domain in the email address. However, this approach fails to account for domain hosters that manage multiple customer domains without publishing configuration settings.

To resolve this issue, we propose an enhancement to explore alternative DNS MX records as a supplementary lookup method. Specifically:

1. If initial lookups fail, query the DNS MX record for the domain in the email address.
2. Extract the top-level domain (TLD) from the MX record (e.g., mx1.dreamhost.com -> dreamhost.com).
3. Re-initiate the autoconfig lookup process with the extracted TLD as the new domain to search, incorporating ISP fetch and Mozilla DB lookups.
4. Determine whether to restart the heuristic process on the original domain or the MX domain (or both), balancing probe speed and connection limits.

This enhancement aims to improve autoconfig lookup success rates for domain hosters by leveraging DNS MX records to identify potential configuration settings.

At present, it is possible to play a system default or user-selected audio file on receiving an email. That's great! For instance, I subscribe to technical groups for Ant, Tomcat, and various other technologies. Also, I get my fair share of spam. I use message filters to delete spam and to file the various emails that result from subscriptions in appropriate folders where I will look at them at my convenience. **Feature Request: Automatic Tab Re-activation on Closure**

**Description:** Upon closing a tab, the application should automatically re-activate the parent tab from which it originated. This behavior would maintain continuity and provide an intuitive user experience when working with multiple tabs.

**Use Case:** When switching between tabs and opening new content within them, the last active tab should remain active even after closing another tab. Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request Title:** Provide Manual Setup Option for Mail Accounts in TB3

**Description:**

The current implementation of adding mail accounts to Thunderbird 3 (TB3) assumes IMAP protocol and does not provide an option for manual setup. This results in users having to stop the account addition process, switch to manual mode, and then proceed with setting up their email account settings manually.

To enhance user experience, a new sequence is proposed:

1. In Account Settings, select "Add Mail" from the dropdown list.
2. Enter name, email address, and password, then click Continue.
3. A popup should appear, asking users to choose between:
	* Automated function: Thunderbird creates settings based on the email address.
	* Manual setup: Users can configure their account settings manually.

When TB 3.0.4 is restarted, it displays the same tabs from when it was closed, and it maintains the same selected tab from when it was closed.

2. Show previous tabs but select the Folders tab by default.

**Request:** Enhance guessConfig() Functionality to Return Both POP3 and IMAP Configurations

The current implementation of the guessConfig() function abruptly terminates as soon as it encounters a high-preference server, prioritizing IMAP over POP3. As a result, only the most preferred server is returned, with no consideration for alternative protocols.

To address this limitation, we propose modifying the guessConfig() function to return both POP3 and IMAP configurations as alternatives when available. The algorithm should only terminate once it has identified servers for both protocols, ensuring that both configurations are considered before returning a result. This update will enable the simultaneous retrieval of POP3 and IMAP settings, meeting the requirements specified in bug 532590 and its related counterpart, bug 556729.

gmail has the [All mail] concept which is intended to obviate mail deletion.
It's typically enormous.

Thunderbird tries to store and index this locally, even when using imap.
This leads to very large [all mail] files, which tend to be very fragmented.
A modest example is an xp machine with a 40Gb hard drive, 6Gb free, [all mail] is 200Mb, 4000 fragments - it's the number of fragments that is the serious problem - there isn't a decent sized chunk of free space anywhere, so defragment doesn't achieve much.
Indexing takes up excessive time and space in global-message-db.sqlite as well.
I'd suggest thunderbird needs controls to better manage files - perhaps downloading headers only for selected folders, setting extension sizes so that folders get expanded say 5mb at a time, rather than message by message. Better selectivity for indexing would be good too.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Title:** Optimized File Management and Indexing for Large Mail Folders

**Description:**

When using IMAP with Gmail, Thunderbird attempts to store and index the "All Mail" folder locally. This results in excessively large files (up to 200MB) with numerous fragments, leading to performance issues and difficulties with disk defragmentation. The indexing process also consumes significant storage space and time.

To mitigate this issue, it is proposed that Thunderbird introduce controls for managing large mail folders, including the ability to:

* Download headers only for selected folders
* Set incremental folder expansion sizes (e.g., 5MB at a time) instead of message-by-message
* Improve selectivity for indexing

Implementing these features would help prevent fragmentation and improve overall performance when dealing with large IMAP mail folders. This enhancement is particularly relevant to users with limited disk space, as observed on Windows platforms.

**Relevance:** Reproducible under certain conditions (Steps to Reproduce provided). Not a bug, but rather a long-term performance issue that warrants optimization.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Feature Request: Per-Contact Default Outgoing Account**

The proposed feature would allow users to associate a default outgoing account with each contact in their address book. This would enable Thunderbird to automatically select the specified account for outgoing emails sent to that contact, overriding the global default and UI focus rules.

**Background**
When sending emails to multiple contacts using different accounts, it is easy to make mistakes or forget to switch back to the correct account. This can lead to confusion, broken conversation tracking, and unintended disclosure of account information.

**Description**
The requested feature would provide a per-contact setting for default outgoing accounts, ensuring that the intended account is used when sending emails to each contact. This would enhance user convenience and prevent common mistakes.

**Relevance**
This issue is not limited to mailing lists and can occur in normal conversations. The proposed solution is related to an existing feature request (Bug 367586) and may be addressed by a third-party plugin (Email Account Manager), but this enhancement request aims to integrate the functionality directly into Thunderbird.

summary: Large, frequently changing files for folders are unfriendly to backups and other system activities
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux x86_64; en-US; rv:1.9.1.9) Gecko/20100330 Fedora/3.5.9-1.fc11 Firefox/3.5.9
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux x86_64; en-US; rv:1.9.1.9) Gecko/20100430 Fedora/3.0.4-2.fc11 Thunderbird/3.0.4

Sorry if this is a dup. It surprises me, but I can't seem to find it
in the database.

Most incremental backup systems work at the granularity of an entire
file. If you modify a 1GB file every day, you'll use 1 GB per day of
backup space and network bandwidth, even if the changes are only a few
MB. That's not very good application behavior.

Fairly common modes of use for Thunderbird lead to large folders that
change frequently. It's not difficult or unusual to end up with folders
gigabytes in size changing on a daily basis, as well as with large
indices and the like which change frequently. Daily backups dutifully
pick up these files, and backup size and bandwidth requirements soar
soar.

For example, my own system is to keep everything in the inbox, and mark
messages read when they're no longer of interest. Left to myself, I'd
never delete anything and never archive anything. Others, like my wife,
do things like putting messages they've dealt with in an archive folder,
which might contain months or years of mail, and might be added to on a
daily basis.

Since folder compaction isn't necessarily automatic (a privacy risk in
itself...), and this isn't obvious to some users, it's also entirely
possible to end up with huge files full of "deleted" messages.

You could argue that:

o It's possible for the user to work around this with lots of little
  folders and the resulting elaborate folder management structure...
  but I submit that that's really asking the user to do the
  application's job for it.

o It's possible for the sysadmin to work around it with special case
  backup code... but it's unreasonable to expect every sysadmin
  to figure out a way to back up your folder structure, or even to
  expect sysadmins to do *anything* special for every single app.
  Especially when "sysadmins" are often more properly called "users".

o Backup systems should be smarter about intra-file incrementality...
  but it's very hard to do that efficiently without knowing something
  about the structure of the files.

o The file system where the backups live should deduplicate them... but

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request for Improved Backup Efficiency**

The current behavior of Thunderbird's file management can lead to inefficient backups due to large, frequently changing files. When users modify or accumulate mail in their inbox or other folders, daily backups consume significant storage space and network bandwidth, even if changes are minor.

To address this issue, we propose that Thunderbird break down large files into smaller, more manageable chunks. This would enable more efficient incremental backups, reducing storage requirements and backup times. Specifically, we suggest using a format such as maildirs or splitting large files into mbox files of approximately 50MB in size.

This enhancement aims to improve user experience by minimizing the impact of frequent file changes on backup systems, while also providing a more scalable solution for sysadmins and users with large mail archives.

**Key Benefits:**

* Reduced storage requirements for backups
* Improved backup efficiency and speed
* Simplified management of large mail archives

**Reproducibility:** This issue is consistently reproducible after extended periods of use with Thunderbird, particularly when users accumulate large amounts of mail in their inbox or other folders.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request:** Modify "Always show remote content from" functionality in Thunderbird to prevent creation of a new contact by default.

**Description:**

When an email contains HTML with remote content, Thunderbird displays a warning frame with options to show or always display remote content. Currently, clicking the "Always show remote content from..." link forces the creation of a new contact unless one is created manually. This behavior is counterintuitive and imposes unnecessary overhead on users who do not want to add every sender to their address book.

**Expected Behavior:**

Upon clicking the "Always show remote content from..." link, Thunderbird should:

1. Add the email address to the safe-filter or a designated list for tracking temporary entries.
2. Prompt the user to confirm whether they would like to add the sender to the address book. This step can be skipped if the email address contains specific keywords (e.g., "noreply@").
3. Optionally, provide an additional contact list or categorization option to manage these temporary entries.

**Rationale:**

This request aims to improve user experience by separating the decision to add a sender to the address book from the decision to display remote content. This change will reduce unnecessary contact creation and enhance overall usability.

summary: Include forwarded messages in conversation view
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Windows; U; Windows NT 5.1; en-US; rv:1.9.2.10) Gecko/20100914 Firefox/3.6.10 (.NET CLR 3.5.30729)
Build Identifier: 

Assume you have an e-mail conversation with person A and at some point in time, you forward a message out of that conversation to person B. This forward is semantically related to the initial conversation with A. If now B starts a conversation based on the forwarded message, we have one semantical conversation. Unfortunately, the conversation view is broken at the time you forward a message and you have to search for the two separate conversations

Reproducible: Always

Steps to Reproduce:
1. Send an email
2. Reply to that email
3. Forward the reply
4. Reply to the forwarded message
Actual Results:  
Messages 1,2 are one conversation.
Messages 3,4 are another conversation.

Expected Results:  
Messages 1-4 should be a single conversation.

If you forward an e-mail message, the composed e-mail does not contain any reference to the message ID of the forwarded message. Therefore, this prevents forwarded messages from being included in the conversation view.

The "References:" header field seems to be appropriate according to RFC 822, "The contents of this field identify other  correspondence which  this message references.  Note that if message identifiers are used, they must use the msg-id specification format."

According to the current RFC 5322, the "References:" header should be used when replying to a message, but the standard does not exclude it to be used in other cases.

I don't know the code, but setting the "References:" header might be the solution to that issue.

Alternatively, one could use a custom "X-Forwards:" header referring to the forwarded message and respect this header when creating the conversation view. This, however, seems to be only the second choice.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Implement a more flexible filter mechanism to combat evolving spammer techniques, particularly those using image-based content without text.

**Problem Statement:**

The existing filter definition mechanism requires lexical filtering methods (e.g., "contains," "starts with"), which may not be sufficient to counter emerging spam tactics. Specifically, current filters are limited in their ability to detect and block image-based spam, such as multipart/mixed attachments containing only a PNG image.

**Requirements:**

1. The new filter mechanism should enable the detection of images without body text.
2. It should allow for more complex filtering conditions, including arithmetic or logical tests (e.g., X-Mozilla-Status2 < 1000000) and lexical matching methods (e.g., "begins with," "ends with").
3. The ability to filter attachments based on size is also desirable.

**Expected Outcome:**

A more flexible and effective filtering system that can adapt to evolving spammer techniques, enabling the efficient blocking of unwanted image-based content.

summary: Improve UI to workaround scam detection generating too many false positives
description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux x86_64; en-US) AppleWebKit/534.13 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/9.0.597.19 Safari/534.13
Build Identifier: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; U; Linux x86_64; en-US; rv:1.9.2.13) Gecko/20101208 Lightning/1.0b2 Thunderbird/3.1.7

Regularly, several times a day, Thunderbird will claim that it thinks "This message may be a scam." It is never clear why it thinks this (it would be good if this was documented somewhere), but so far it has never been right. I've had dozens of such warnings for perfectly legitimate emails, and *not once* have I had it for an actual scam.

This means that the detection logic is apparently bad at detecting actual scams and has been degraded so much in order to make it catch some actual scams that it generates an enormous amounts of false positives in the process. This makes it completely useless, since nobody will believe it anymore when it says a message may be a scam. It's the "boy who cried wolf" syndrome.

The net effect on security is probably negative. People who don't rely on it gain no extra security, while people who do rely on it may not themselves scrutinize messages enough anymore and may therefore be more likely to be deceived by one of the many scams not detected by Thunderbird.

This is a hard problem. Any time the positives far outnumber the negatives an algorithm that generates even a small percentage of false positives will be useless. I think the scam detection should therefore be turned off, or vastly improved (which I don't think is possible).

Reproducible: Sometimes

Steps to Reproduce:
Monitor incoming messages.
Actual Results:  
Many legitimate messages will be labelled as scams, and very few actual scams will be.

Expected Results:  
Legitimate messages should not be marked as scams, and actual scams should be.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Enhance User Interface to Improve False Positive Detection in Scam Alert System

The current implementation of the scam detection system generates excessive false positives, causing legitimate emails to be mislabeled as potential scams. This has resulted in diminished user trust and potentially compromised security, as users may become complacent and less vigilant when receiving these warnings. To address this issue, we propose either disabling or significantly improving the scam detection algorithm to minimize false positives and maintain accurate threat identification.

**Key Issues:**

* Excessive false positives lead to decreased effectiveness of the scam alert system
* Legitimate emails are frequently mislabeled as potential scams
* Actual scams may not be detected due to the degraded performance of the algorithm

**Desired Outcome:**

* Improve the accuracy of the scam detection system to minimize false positives and ensure legitimate emails are not flagged incorrectly.
* Enhance user trust in the security features by reducing unnecessary warnings and alarms.

There are two ways to send and S/MIME message in an encrypted way:
a) set the "Default encryption setting when sending messages:" to "Required" (in the Account Security Settings).
b) manually activate encryption by enabling "Encrypt This Message" in the S/MIME menu when composing a message

Both possibilities have disadvantages if a user does not S/MIME encrypt 100% of his outgoing emails: 
(a) is in the most cases not feasible as many outgoing emails still will be unencrypted and a user would need to disable the encryption before being able to send unencrypted messages (this impacts the user experience seriously).

Manually activating encryption per message (b) brings along the high risk to send a message accidentally in an unencrypted manner.


Therefore I would suggest to implement per-recipient rules for S/MIME as it is already implemented by the Enigmail extension for GPG/PGP only:
http://enigmail.mozdev.org/documentation/pgprules.php.html

This enhancement would improve 
- the user experience for S/MIME users because after the creation of a per-recipient rule no manual intervention is required
- the security, by reducing the risk of accidentally sending messages unencrypted

**Enhancement Request:** Composing Messages with Per-Recipient S/MIME Settings

**Purpose:** Implement per-recipient rules for S/MIME settings to improve user experience and security when sending encrypted messages.

**Background:** Currently, users have two options to send S/MIME encrypted messages: setting the default encryption setting or manually enabling encryption on a per-message basis. However, both methods have limitations that can lead to unencrypted messages being sent accidentally.

**Proposal:** Introduce per-recipient rules for S/MIME settings, similar to those implemented by the Enigmail extension for GPG/PGP. This would allow users to create specific encryption settings for each recipient, eliminating the need for manual intervention and reducing the risk of sending unencrypted messages.

**Benefits:** This enhancement would improve user experience for S/MIME users by streamlining the encryption process and enhance security by minimizing the risk of accidental unencrypted message transmission.

**Benefits:**

This feature is considered relatively simple to implement and would enhance the overall usability and security of the system.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Issue:** Inability to stop download and compact large mail folders when size limit is reached

**Description:**

When attempting to download a large amount of email messages, Thunderbird fails to provide a way to interrupt the download process when a mail folder reaches its size limit. Additionally, the "Compact Folder" feature does not function as expected on affected folders.

**Specific Issues:**

1. When the size limit is reached, the warning dialog prevents further downloads, but there is no way to exit the process without abruptly closing Thunderbird.
2. After exiting and restarting Thunderbird, compacting the affected folder fails, causing an infinite loop of attempting to recreate the index file.

**Proposed Solutions:**

1. Implement a mechanism to allow users to interrupt the download process when a mail folder reaches its size limit.
2. Modify the compact feature to successfully compact large folders that have reached their size limit.

**Additional Observations:**

* The size limit on Linux platforms appears to be misconfigured, allowing folders to exceed 2GB in size.
* An abrupt exit of Thunderbird may cause filtering issues or missing emails in the Inbox.

description:
User-Agent:       Mozilla/5.0 (Macintosh; U; Intel Mac OS X 10_6_6; en-us) AppleWebKit/533.19.4 (KHTML, like Gecko) Version/5.0.3 Safari/533.19.4

I have received a long thread of emails (replies, forwarded) with the same subject.

Usually, replies are prefixed with "Re:" and forwarded emails are prefixed with "FW:", and FF correctly groups them together when I sort them by subject.

However, non-English versions of Microsoft Outlook prefix their replies by localized forms, e.g. "AW:" (Antwort) for reply in German, or "ODP:" (odpowiedzi) in Polish, or "WG:" (weitergeleitet) for forwarded in German.

If emails from those Outlook clients are part of an email thread, FF can't identify them as related, with the consequence that this thread disintegrates into several ones.

The thread contains a lot of "different" subject lines, like:

"Original Subject"
"AW: Original Subject"
"AW: Re: Original Subject"
"Re: AW: Original Subject"
"FW: Re: AW: Original Subject"
"Re: ODP: FW: WG: Re: AW: Original Subject"
"Re: AW: Re: AW: Re: AW: Re: AW: Re: AW: Re: AW: Original Subject"
etc.

FF groups them only so far as traversing through the leading Re's and FW's.

A message with subject "AW: Original Subject" ends up somewhere entirely else alphabetically than "Original Subject"

It would be helpful if FF were able to identify all these prefixes and ignore them. Or perhaps it should just ignore any 2- or 3-letter words followed by a colon, but this could have lots of side-effects.

In this mozillazine forum discussion, outlook was identified as the culprit, so no action was taken: http://forums.mozillazine.org/viewtopic.php?f=30&t=62942

But the way I see it, FF would greatly improve my user experience if it cold sort these emails correctly.

Concerning standard compliance:

RFC 5322 says that "Re:" MAY be prefixed in replies, but it doesn't say that "AW:" must not.

Apparently, Outlook doesn't add a "In-Reply-To:"  or "Reference:" header, which it SHOULD do, and which could be used instead of the subject.

Reproducible: Always

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request for Improved Subject-Based Sorting**

The Thunderbird email client should enhance its ability to recognize and ignore localized prefixes added by Microsoft Outlook when sorting messages by subject. Currently, non-English versions of Outlook prefix replies with unique characters (e.g., "AW:", "ODP:", or "WG:") instead of the standard "Re:". As a result, emails in a thread are not correctly identified as related, causing them to be sorted separately.

This issue can lead to disintegration of email threads into multiple groups within an inbox. To address this problem, Thunderbird should be able to detect and ignore these localized prefixes or any short words followed by a colon (:) when sorting messages. This enhancement will improve the user experience for users who receive emails from non-English Outlook clients.

**Background**

This issue is related to the standard compliance of email headers. While RFC 5322 allows "Re:" in replies, it does not prohibit other prefixes. However, Microsoft Outlook should be adding required headers ("In-Reply-To:" or "Reference:") instead of relying on unique subject prefixes.

**Severity and Reproducibility**

This issue is consistently reproducible across different scenarios and email threads.

description:

Currently, when you do an advanced search in Thunderbird, you have a set of fields to choose, and + - buttons to add them or more criteria lines, each criterion line being made of Field Operator Value (e.g. Subject Contains "Mozilla")

But in almost all cases, a person will search only using a small subset of these fields - ie. From, To, Subject, Body, Age, Date, Attachment Status

It would enormously enhance the user experience when a search is called up, if these frequent fields were pre-entered as a vertical list with blanks for their values (Date occurring twice, with is before and is after for its methods), so that all a person does for searching, is click into them and type. If they want other fields, they can obviously use the + button.

To have such a prepopulated field list, one would need to have it so that a field with a blank value is skipped and not used to build the search criterion equation. Currently, if you have "Date is before (blank)" or any field with blank, then the whole search results returns nothing, which no one ever wants. If autoconfig is used with an XML file on a web server, it is very limited in using a selection of incoming and outgoing servers. If e.g. a server offers IMAP and IMAPS, only the first entry will be shown in the autoconfig dialog. This also applies if e.g. SMTPS and SMTP/STARTTLS are both available.

Particularly, between SMTPS and SMTP/STARTTLS there isn't any difference in terms of security. The two should be offered as alternatives only defaulting to one.

Whenever a secure (SSL encrypted) and an insecure service are available, autoconfig should either default to the secure service or (preferably) read a global policy argument from the XML as well which tells it how to handle that situation (ban insecure, default to secure/insecure). That way the order of services in the XML becomes irrelevant.

What would make Thunderbird the best IMAP client in the world would be the following:

1. In the IMAP subscription dialog, the user should be able to specify what the logical use of each physical folder should be. Here I could specify that the physical "INBOX.Sent" is logically a sent mail folder, or in the Hungarian server, "Elküldött" is also logically a sent mail folder.

2. This configuration could be included in the public mail server database, too, but only as a default, so that it's customizable, too. Also there could be global common mappings, like "Sent", "Sent mail", "Sent items" are usual names for the same logical thing.

So, each physical-logical mapping could have 2 attributes: physical folder -> logical use and name alias.

Most users would place a copy of sent mails under the logical sent folder, and that's a sensible default, but that can be changed to anything else. **Description:** The current "Reply" functionality for RSS items in Thunderbird is limited. 3. Launch a browser to view the full item

The topic classification was only a secondary criteria (inside the "high books", all high books of maths were together, but small books of maths were elsewhere). description:
+++ This bug was initially created as a clone of Bug #229224 +++

Bug 229224 implements the functionality of reordering attachments during composition, made accessible via drag & drop for mouse users only.

This bug adds keyboard accessibility for reordering attachments.

STR

0 After bug 229224 is fixed...
1 Compose message, add 3 or more attachments
2 Select one or more attachments and try to move them up/down within the list of attachments using keyboard only

Current Result:
- reordering of attachments is not keyboard accessible

Expected Result:
- reordering of attachments must be keyboard accessible

Suggested Implementation:

A: Shortcut keys
For selected and focussed attachment(s) only(!):

Note that the following shortcut keys will only apply when
- there is more than 1 attachment
- focus is in attachment list and
- one or more attachments are selected

A1: [Alt]+[Cursor up] to move attachment(s) up within the list
    [Alt]+[Cursor down] to move attachment(s) down within the list

- A1 is the most important functionality, as it allows for simple, intuitive and and efficient reordering of attachments via keyboard (a must for disabled users; greater speed and precision than drag&drop for all users).
- We cannot use any other modifier keys as they are taken:
Ctrl is for selection (at least on Win)
Shift is for selection (at least on Win).
So [Alt] is the only option, and it's also somewhat intuitive if you think of
alt-eration of the position.
- [Alt]+Cursor keys is not used for anything else in the composer window

A2: [Alt]+[Pos1] to move attachment(s) to the beginning of the list
    [Alt]+[End] to move attachment(s) to the end of the list

- A2 would be the logical extension of A1 to fast-track moving attachments to the beginning or end of the list.
- intuitive, as Pos1 and End will move focus (and selection) to the beginning/end of the list; combined with [Alt], it's moving list items to the same positions.

**Request:** Enhance Attachment Detachment with Robust Linking Mechanism

**Description:**
When detaching attachments from messages, save both a soft link and a hard link (or Alias/Shortcut) to the file. This will provide a more robust linking mechanism that can withstand common actions like renaming files or moving them between folders.

**Rationale:**
The existing attachment detachment process relies on a fragile soft link, which can break if the file is modified or relocated. By storing hard link information, we can ensure that attachments remain accessible even after changes to their location or name.

**Implementation:**

1. During attachment detachment, retrieve and store both soft link and hard link (or Alias/Shortcut) information available on the platform.
2. When resolving a detachment link, attempt to use the stored hard link record if the soft link fails.

**Benefits:**
This enhancement will improve attachment linking robustness, ensuring that attachments remain accessible even after changes to their location or name. This is particularly useful for POP and IMAP accounts, as it can provide information about the machine where the attachment resides, facilitating remote mounting of volumes.

**Description:** The user experience can be significantly improved by implementing a feature to efficiently detect and identify memory-leaking add-ons within Firefox. * Optimize system resource allocation
* Enhance overall browsing experience

1. Install a variety of popular and less popular Firefox extensions, as well as standard video playing codecs and plugins.
2. Engage in typical browsing activities, such as using FireBug and watching videos for an extended period.
3. Observe system resource utilization metrics (e.g., memory usage and CPU usage).
4. Restart Firefox with all pages saved on quit.

**Expected Outcome:** A feature that rapidly detects and identifies memory-leaking add-ons, allowing users to efficiently troubleshoot and mitigate performance issues related to excessive memory usage.

summary: sqlite3_trace logging is pathologically bad news for FTS3 users on debug builds
description:
Created attachment 505716
sucks to be someone who knows how to dynamically change log levels v1

I posted the following to the sqlite-users, list.  Here's a link in case there's a follow-up or anything:
http://www.mail-archive.com/sqlite-users@sqlite.org/msg58266.html

And here's the body, enclosing in equals signs:
===========================================================================
In our Mozilla debug builds we use sqlite3_trace to expose the SQL 
statements that are invoked via our PR_LOG logging subsystem.  This 
usually works out well but the trace also catches FTS3's statements in 
its net.  During a segment merge, a segment in a Thunderbird FTS3 table 
can easily be >100k.

Unfortunately, the calls to stringify the BLOB end up growing the string 
"%02x" character by "%02x" character, and sqlite3StrAccumAppend grows 
its allocation size linearly and without using realloc.  This results in 
a tremendous number of calls to the allocator and a lot of memory 
traffic (both copying and memsetting).

While this is definitely one of those "well, don't do that" cases, I 
think it would be beneficial if one or more of the following were to 
occur, if only because it would be nice to not have to turn 
sqlite3_trace off on any connection that uses FTS3.

1) Cause FTS3 statements to not generate OP_Trace codes or to ignore 
them during evaluation.
2) Use realloc in sqlite3StrAccumAppend so the memory allocator has a 
fighting chance.  (With the large segment sizes at play, the mozilla 
jemalloc, for example, ends up unmapping things at least some of the time.)
3) Use a more efficient BLOB stringification routine.
4) Allow not stringifying BLOBs at all.
5) Place an upper bound or allow the sqlite3_trace invocation to place 
an upper bound on how large the SQL string can grow.

It's very survivable if none of the above ever happen, too.

Here's a snippet of an unhappy stack using the 3.7.4 amalgamation in the 
off-chance it helps provide better context:
#7  sqlite3Malloc (n=264183) at sqlite3/src/sqlite3.c:17763
#8  sqlite3DbMallocRaw (db=ptr, n=264183) at sqlite3.c:18088
#9  sqlite3StrAccumAppend (p=ptr, z=ptr, N=2) at sqlite3.c:19002
#10 sqlite3VXPrintf (pAccum=ptr, useExtended=1, fmt=ptr "x", 
ap=0x7fcaba7fc8e0) at sqlite3.c:18952
#11 sqlite3XPrintf (p=ptr, zFormat=ptr "%02x") at sqlite3.c:19241
#12 sqlite3VdbeExpandSql (p=ptr, zRawSql=ptr ")") at sqlite3.c:59748
#13 sqlite3VdbeExec (p=0x7fcaac70c5d8) at sqlite3.c:66203
#14 sqlite3Step (p=ptr) at sqlite3.c:58704
#15 sqlite3_step (pStmt=ptr) at sqlite3.c:58768
#16 fts3WriteSegment (p=ptr, iBlock=ptr, z=ptr "", n=166139) at 
sqlite3.c:115871
===========================================================================

We automatically activate sqlite3_trace on all debug builds in Connection::initialize regardless of the actual state of logging.  While it would be preferable if we could only activate sqlite3_trace if logging is actually activated, it is within the power of native in-tree consumers to safely, if evilly, cast mozIStorageConnection to Connection, gain access to the sqlite3* instance and then just turn the logging off for themselves.  (I have a patch for Thunderbird to do this, if needed.)

I propose the following:

1) Spin off a bug wherein we use PR_LOG_TEST to decide whether to tell sqlite3_trace to turn on in the first place.  I am attaching the patch that we would associate with that bug to this bug in the off-chance a braver person than I is willing to fight the good fight required to land this on mozilla-central in the near future.

2) Leave this bug around as a warning to others until something happens upstream that stops sqlite3_trace from being dangerous to FTS3 users on debug builds.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Improve SQLite logging performance for FTS3 users in debug builds

**Background:** In Mozilla's debug builds, the `sqlite3_trace` feature is enabled by default, which can lead to significant performance issues with FTS3 tables due to excessive memory allocation and stringification of BLOBs.

**Proposed Improvements:**

1. **Optimize SQLite logging for FTS3**: Modify the behavior of FTS3 statements to avoid generating `OP_Trace` codes or ignore them during evaluation.
2. **Improve memory allocation efficiency**: Use `realloc` in `sqlite3StrAccumAppend` to reduce the number of calls to the allocator and minimize memory traffic.
3. **Enhance BLOB stringification routine**: Implement a more efficient method for converting BLOBs to strings.
4. **Allow optional BLOB stringification**: Provide an option to skip stringifying BLOBs altogether.

**Current Workaround:** The current solution involves disabling `sqlite3_trace` on connections that use FTS3 tables, which is not ideal.

**Proposed Next Steps:**

1. Create a separate bug to implement the `PR_LOG_TEST` logic for enabling/disabling `sqlite3_trace`.
2. Leave this bug open as a warning to others until upstream changes address the performance issues related to SQLite logging and FTS3 on debug builds.

This description summarizes the key points from the original request, focusing on the main issue (performance issues with FTS3 in debug builds) and the proposed improvements. It uses professional language and avoids direct re-use of the original wording.

**Request:** Enhance Add-on Manager with View Selection Options

**Description:**

To improve user experience in the Add-on Manager, we propose introducing view selection options, similar to those found in Windows Explorer. This enhancement would provide users with flexibility to choose from multiple display modes, including:

1. **Icon View**: Display add-ons as icons with name and version information.
2. **List View**: Show a list of add-ons with icon, name, and version details, as well as currently available buttons.
3. **Details View**: Provide a detailed view of each add-on, including Add-on ID, most recent install or update date, and sortable fields.

In all views, users should be able to right-click on an add-on for quick access to key options, such as:

* Navigation to the add-on's settings
* Enable/Disable toggle
* View additional information about the add-on

This enhancement aims to provide users with a more intuitive and customizable experience when managing their add-ons.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Request:** Enable Restartless Add-ons with XPCOM Components via Chrome Manifest

**Description:**

This enhancement aims to allow restartless add-ons in Mozilla to utilize both binary and JavaScript XPCOM components, with support for loading these components through a chrome manifest file. The primary objectives are to address lifecycle issues related to cached XPCOM components, ensure safe loading and unloading of binary components, and provide a mechanism for loading custom XPT interfaces.

**Key Challenges:**

1. Lifetime and lifecycle management for cached XPCOM components
2. Safe loading and unloading of binary components with outstanding reference counts
3. Loading custom XPT interfaces

**Theoretical Solutions:** While possible via manual calls to nsIComponentRegistrar and js-ctypes, these approaches are considered fragile and undocumented.

**Dependency:** This enhancement is dependent on bug 564667 (Allow bootstrapped add-ons to have chrome), which would simplify the implementation by enabling the parsing of chrome manifests or allowing bootstrap.js to trigger manifest parsing at startup and shutdown.

summary: Allow cancelling async requests
description:
An occasional problem with async requests is that the user can close a window that is still waiting for a response, then you end up with weird errors about missing Components etc.

We should extend the API to support cancelling async operations. This can be achieved be returning something like an nsICancelable from the appropriate methods. **Functional Enhancement Request**

To enable seamless automatic updates in environments utilizing SSL-inspecting proxies, we propose implementing a secure update signing mechanism. This feature would prevent proxy certificate mismatches from disrupting update processes for Firefox users.

**Background:**

Regulated enterprises frequently deploy SSL-inspecting proxies to ensure network security. However, when attempting to update Firefox, the browser encounters an SSL certificate mismatch due to the proxy's trusted certificate not matching the expected one.

**Problem Statement:**

The current auto-update process is incompatible with SSL-inspecting proxies, resulting in unsuccessful updates and misleading error messages. This issue can be resolved by implementing a secure update signing mechanism that relies on digital signatures rather than transport security.

**Rationale:**

This enhancement will ensure that automatic updates are permitted by proxy rules while maintaining the integrity of network security measures. By signing updates, we can prevent potential exploits and provide users with uninterrupted access to critical security patches and feature enhancements.

**Functional Requirements:**

1. Integrate a secure update signing mechanism into Firefox's auto-update process.
2. Ensure compatibility with SSL-inspecting proxies by verifying signed updates against proxy certificates.

This rewritten description clearly conveys the main purpose of the enhancement request, provides context for the issue, and outlines the proposed solution in a concise and professional manner.

summary: ability to launch a new FF instance from desktop icon when using -no-remote
description:
In windows, the default "standard" behavior for all other browsers besides FF is that if I double-click the browser icon, I get a new window instance popped up (whether I already have one or more open, or that's the first instance). This allows each browser instance to occupy its own entry on the windows taskbar. In this way, a user can have multiple window instances open, each with its own set of tabs, etc, and easily switch between them using standard windows navigation (via taskbar mouse interaction, alt+tab, etc).

For FF, however, a special wrinkle makes this more difficult. For a web developer that has multiple versions of FF installed (I have 3.5, 3.6, 4, and nightly), to be able to open those up side-by-side (a common need in web-dev), I have to use "-no-remote" and "-P xx" command-line parameters to start up each version of FF with a different profile.

This works fine. But it has the unfortunate side effect that it means a catch-22, where now the desktop icon can't be used to launch new instances of the window if one instance (of that version) is already open. On windows, I get the "Firefox is already running, but is not responding. To open a new window, you must first close the existing Firefox process, or restart your system."

What *is* possible is that in an open instance (of any version), a user can do "Ctrl+N" to open a new window instance. But what I am requesting is some way to accomplish that "open new window" functionality from the desktop icon.

The catch-22 is that "-no-remote" is used to prevent the "FF3.6" icon from just connecting to and launching a new instance of an already open FF4 process. But with remoting disabled, double-clicking the desktop icon provides no way to communicate with an existing instance of the matching version, and do this "open new window" functionality that I would like to have.

So, I guess my request really boils down to this: I'd like to have an alternate command-line option to "-no-remote" which is more like "-remote-only-same-version". It would serve to allow remoting only if the launching version of the browser matches an existing running version. This would preserve being able to launch FF3.6 side-by-side with FF4 (using diff profiles), but if a second instance of either running version is requested, then remoting could then allow: "Hey, running FF instance that matches my same version, please go ahead and launch a new window instance, because the user clicked the desktop icon again."

To improve the usability and security of the extension installation process, we propose modifying the Add-on Manager (AMO) to display an install dialog before initiating the download of the XPI file. This enhancement would involve providing the necessary information for the dialog as part of the `InstallTrigger` call, ensuring accurate representation of the extension's details.

The current implementation allows certain combinations of add-ons to coexist, resulting in instability, crashes, hangs, and poor user experience. Specifically, the overlapping features of add-ons like FlashBlock, Adblock Plus, and NoScript can cause issues.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request for Isolation Mode in Add-ons**

To facilitate troubleshooting of problematic add-ons, we propose introducing an "Isolation Mode" feature. This mode would allow users to individually enable or disable specific add-ons while keeping all others active. The goal is to streamline the process of identifying performance issues caused by individual add-ons.

**Key Requirements:**

1. Ability to isolate a single add-on for testing and debugging purposes.
2. Automatic, isolated testing of an add-on's performance without uninstalling other add-ons.
3. Two lists of disabled add-ons:
	* One list would display the current isolation mode, allowing users to quickly identify which add-ons are currently being tested.
	* The second list would show a history of add-ons that were previously disabled due to incompatibility with the latest Firefox version, along with the date and time of disablement.

**Benefits:**

1. Improved troubleshooting efficiency for developers and end-users alike.
2. Enhanced collaboration between add-on developers and the Firefox community.
3. Simplified maintenance of add-ons during frequent Firefox updates.

This feature would build upon existing functionality in other software applications (e.g., Adobe Illustrator, DigiDesign's Pro Tools) that offer isolation modes or "sandboxing" capabilities for individual components.

summary: Add telemetry for startup crash detection
description:
Startup crash detection was added in bug 294260.  I think the following pieces of telemetry data would be useful:

1) The uptime when start crash tracking began and ended.
** This is so we can measure the proportion of startup crashes that the feature
   detects by comparing with uptime data in crash-stats.
2) Whether the user was forced into safe mode by the startup crash detection.
** This would let us know how useful this feature is: to know if/when people are
   experiencing N consecutive startup crashes (where N is currently 3).
3) Whether the last startup was a crash.
** This would only be recorded if we didn't crash on the following startup since
   it seems telemetry data is only saved at shutdown.  Could I have telemetry
   save to disk in this case?
** It would be nice to know the number of consecutive startup crashes but then
   we'd be counting users more than once with every additional crash.

There are problems collecting some of this data if there is a crash before telemetry is sent or persisted on disk. Any suggestions?

Note that the startup crash detection may detect some crashes which breakpad doesn't but it can only increment the counter if startup reaches the point where it begins tracking.  #2 & #3 will be useful to compare to Socorro data.

Is it necessary to call accumulate with a false value for boolean telemetry when we just want to know how often something happens ie. #2?  From what I can tell it should be enough to just report the interesting (true) case and then compare that to the number of telemetry reports for the time period.  This is what Telemetry::A11Y_INSTANTIATED currently does but it leads to useless bar graphs showing 100% of reporters with it on without showing the total number of reports that didn't specify a value.  It seems like boolean telemetry probes should have a default value.  The advantage of only reporting in the true case is that it has no perf. impact.

**Telemetry Enhancement Request: Startup Crash Detection**

We propose collecting additional telemetry data to improve understanding and analysis of startup crash detection performance. Specifically, we aim to gather metrics on the proportion of startup crashes detected by the feature, user interactions with safe mode, and consecutive startup crashes.

The following telemetry data will be collected:

1. Uptime when start crash tracking began and ended
2. Whether users are forced into safe mode due to startup crashes
3. Consecutive startup crashes (with consideration for avoiding duplicate counting)

To address potential issues with collecting data in case of a pre-existing crash, we may need to persist telemetry data on disk at appropriate intervals.

This enhancement will help compare the effectiveness of startup crash detection with Socorro data and inform optimization efforts. We also aim to explore alternative approaches for reporting boolean telemetry values, such as introducing default values to reduce performance impact while maintaining informative bar graphs.

summary: Improve SafeBrowsing store SubPrefix compression
description:
I've been keeping an eye on the growth of the SafeBrowsing database to be sure everything is working OK, and one thing that gets to me is the size of the malware files. When originally working on this thing, I thought that AddPrefixes and AddChunks were the important thing, and we'd get everything down to about 2.4M. And this is right, for the phishing list. The malware list is another matter:

2012-02-24 05:55:40.431215 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]: Table goog-malware-shavar now has:
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431234 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   12846 add chunks
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431239 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   386464 add prefixes
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431242 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   1 add completions
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431254 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   10562 sub chunks
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431257 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   226033 sub prefixes
2012-02-24 05:55:40.431259 UTC - 1657325312[7f546462b9c0]:   1 sub completions

The amount of sub prefixes is over half the total amount. We currently use zlib (DEFLATE) on the chunk numbers (of which sub prefixes have 2), and store the sub prefixes uncompressed (mostly because PrefixSet doesn't have stream serialization support, and I didn't anticipate there being so many in the first place).

Because the chunk data only spans a small amount of numbers (+-13000, see above), I did a quick hack to store them delta-encoded. To my surprise, this *worsened* the compression. After looking at it a bit more, I realized 2 issues:

a) Because DEFLATE requires matches with length at least 3 to compress well, it will only be useful for consecutive numbers that aren't more than 256 apart.
b) The data is stored in prefix order, which means the chunk numbers are purely random. This means (a) will almost always fail.

This in turn lead to the following comment in HashStore::WriteSubPrefixes:
  // chunk-ordered prefixes are not compressible

This was true at some point, but before the coded landed, I actually rewrote it to have everything work on the data in prefix order, and hence avoid a whole bunch of re-sorting that was otherwise necessary.

But this does mean that the prefixes should be compressible now. And so should the chunk numbers, if we're a bit smarter.

I kept the DEFLATE backend because we already have it and it does nice things such as huffman coding for us, but added a very simply preprocessing step that splits all 32-bit values into 4 8-bit slices. Because the MSB of our chunkdata is almost all identical, and for example the prefixes, which are sorted, will also have long runs of identical values, compressibility gains a lot. It also avoids the DEFLATE-needs-a-length-3-match problem entirely. And it's fast. Win!

These are the test results on the current database. ShortSlice was a try with splitting the 32-bit data into 2 x 16-bit values, which makes it behave very close to PrefixSet.

https://docs.google.com/spreadsheet/ccc?key=0AiObroK0ZHF-dGFmZWhKLVdSWnhYcGk1VDZaZjg3X1E#gid=0

This reduces our SafeBrowsing store from about 5.5M to 4.5M.

Here is a standardized description of the enhancement request:

**Enhancement Request: Improved SubPrefix Compression for SafeBrowsing Store**

The current implementation of subprefix compression in the SafeBrowsing store has been optimized to reduce its size and improve performance. The major optimization focus was on the malware list, which accounted for most of the storage space.

**Problem Statement:**

* The original approach using zlib (DEFLATE) compression did not effectively compress the large number of sub prefixes due to their random and non-consecutive nature.
* A subsequent attempt at storing chunk data in delta-encoded format actually worsened the compression.

**Solution:**

* Developed a preprocessing step that splits 32-bit values into 4 x 8-bit slices, taking advantage of identical MSB values and long runs of identical values in the chunk data.
* Utilized this split data with an existing DEFLATE backend, which includes Huffman coding benefits.
* Implemented a simple and fast solution to address the DEFLATE's need for length-3 matches.

**Results:**

* Reduced the SafeBrowsing store size from approximately 5.5M to 4.5M.
* Provided test results demonstrating the effectiveness of this optimization approach, compared with alternative methods (e.g., ShortSlice).

This enhancement request aims to further improve the compression efficiency and reduce storage requirements for the SafeBrowsing store, enhancing overall system performance.

Here is a standardized description that clearly conveys the request's main purpose and details:

**Request for Enhanced Password Management on Sites with Hidden Username Fields**

The password manager fails to auto-fill passwords on websites that conceal the username field, such as accounts.google.com. This occurs when attempting to log in to multiple accounts on the same site.

When a user has created multiple accounts on a website without a visible username field (e.g., Google or certain banks), the password manager is unable to fill in the correct password. To address this issue, it would be beneficial to provide an interface that allows users to insert passwords for known logins, even if the username is not explicitly displayed.

**Proposed Solution:**

A possible solution is to introduce a feature in the password manager's popup menu (accessible by right-clicking on the password field) that displays a list of known logins for the current site. When selecting a login, the corresponding password would be inserted into the password field. For unknown usernames or passwords, alternative display options could include:

* Displaying "UNKNOWN USER 1", "UNKNOWN USER 2", etc.
* Showing the first few characters of the password followed by asterisks (e.g., "foo********")

This enhancement would improve user experience and convenience when managing multiple accounts on sites with hidden username fields.

summary: Recover from -wal and -shm files being directories in OpenUnsharedDatabase error handling logic
description:
In bug 750781 in Thunderbird, it was discovered that sometimes, somehow, (probably involving a seriously messed up anti-virus software), the Places -wal and -shm files end up as directories.  In versions of SQLite prior to 3.7.12 (not yet released), error handling retry code would burn a lot of cycles trying to wait out a virus checker because it thought the problem was that the files were actual files but being touched by some other process.  SQLite 3.7.12 will detect the file is a directory and fail immediately.

It is desirable to clean up these messed up directories, and to do so without introducing any file stats in normal operation.  Happily, it appears we should be able to detect the error in OpenUnsharedDatabase only when it's a problem, and then detect and delete these rogue folders.  Since the problem is theorized to be bad anti-virus software, and that can happen to anyone, mozStorage seems like the appropriate location to deal with this.

A realistic test would likely need to create a new database, invoke "PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL", close the database, create the bogus directories, then re-open the database at which point the error cascade should be triggered and we verify success by a successful open and the directories disappearing.  The fix would want to land now, but the test would want to hang out on the tracker bug for planning to land when we take SQLite 3.7.12 or higher.  (The fix is beneficial even with the current version of SQLite, since it will at least avoid the problem from recurring on next startup or next time places tries to initialize itself, etc.)

**Enhancement Request:**

**Title:** Improve Error Handling for -wal and -shm File Corruption

**Description:**

The error handling logic in OpenUnsharedDatabase needs enhancement to recover from cases where the Places -wal and -shm files are unexpectedly converted into directories. This issue can be triggered by malicious anti-virus software, causing SQLite to incorrectly treat these files as being modified externally.

To address this problem, we aim to detect and resolve corrupted directory issues without introducing unnecessary file statistics during normal operation. The proposed solution involves updating the OpenUnsharedDatabase error handling logic to detect and delete rogue directories when they occur, utilizing mozStorage for this purpose.

**Test Plan:**

A realistic test will involve creating a new database with WAL journal mode enabled, closing it, corrupting the -wal and -shm files as directories, and then re-opening the database. Success will be confirmed by a successful database open and the removal of the corrupted directories.

**Implementation Timeline:**

The fix should be implemented immediately to prevent recurrence of this issue on subsequent startups or Places initialization attempts. However, the test plan will remain in the tracker bug until we can ensure compatibility with SQLite 3.7.12 or higher, at which point the fix will be finalized and landed.

Here's a standardized description that clearly conveys the enhancement request's main purpose and details:

**Feature Request: Buffering Module for Asynchronous Function Calls**

We propose creating a reusable module called `BufferingUtils.jsm` to encapsulate functionality for buffering asynchronous function calls with timeout. This module, inspired by the existing `Lazy` class in `SearchService.jsm`, will enable developers to delay and debounce function invocations.

**Key Behavior:**

*   Create a buffered call instance with a specified timeout (DELAY)
*   Invoke the `go()` method to initiate the deferred function call
*   If no subsequent calls to `go()` occur within the specified DELAY, the function is executed after the timer expires
*   If another call to `go()` is made before the timer expires, it is reset

**Potential Use Cases:**

*   Reducing disk access frequency in data-intensive operations (e.g., nsSearchService)
*   Buffering writes with OS.File for improved performance and responsiveness
*   Debouncing UI-related events or interactions (e.g., bug 743069)

This feature will be made available in the toolkit/, enabling developers to leverage this utility across various components and projects.

**Priority Adjustment for Background Transactions**

Update the network priority classification for blocklist and addon checker transactions in background processes to "low" in Necko. This change aims to enhance channel prioritization by providing more granular control over resource requests, allowing for further experimentation and measurement of performance.

**Background:**
The current default priority assignment for these background tasks does not take into account the differing levels of importance between UI-related activities (e.g., stylesheets, JavaScript, HTML) and background processes. By reclassifying these transactions to "low" priority, we can evaluate the impact of pausing or throttling them during high-priority resource retrieval.

This change is expected to have a longer-term effect on performance optimization, as it enables more nuanced prioritization and measurement strategies for resource requests in Necko.
